question: Which of the following observations from Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment led to the conclusion that most of the atom's volume is empty?
option_1: A few alpha particles were deflected by 180°.
option_2: Alpha particles were attracted towards electrons in the atom.
option_3: Some alpha particles were deflected by small angles.
option_4: Most of the alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Most of the alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment, a thin gold foil (about 0.00004 cm thick) was bombarded with fast-moving alpha particles. Most of the particles passed straight through undeflected, which showed that most of the space inside an atom is empty. (रदरफोर्ड का प्रयोग — अधिकांश कण सीधे निकल गए)

 

• A small fraction of alpha particles were deflected through small angles, showing that the positive charge is concentrated in a small region, and a very few (about 1 in 20,000) bounced back at nearly 180°, which led Rutherford to conclude that all the positive charge and most of the mass of the atom are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.

 

• From this experiment Rutherford proposed the nuclear model of the atom: a small, dense, positively charged nucleus at the centre, with electrons revolving around it in the mostly empty space of the atom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The deflection of some particles at small angles indicated the positive charge concentrated in the nucleus, while the deflection of a few particles at 180° indicated the nucleus is very small and dense compared to the size of the atom.

 

• Rutherford's model could not explain the stability of the atom, since an accelerating electron should radiate energy and spiral into the nucleus; this defect was later resolved by Bohr's model.

 

NOTE

 

• A few alpha particles deflected by 180° (Option A): This observation shows that the nucleus is small and dense (concentrates the positive charge and mass), not that the atom is mostly empty.

 

• Alpha particles attracted towards electrons (Option B): This did not happen; electrons are far too light to deflect a heavy alpha particle.

 

• Some alpha particles deflected by small angles (Option C): This shows the presence of a positively charged nucleus repelling the alpha particles, not that the atom is mostly empty.

question: Which of the following tissues have contractile proteins that contract and relax to cause movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muscular tissue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muscular tissue is made up of elongated cells called muscle fibres, which contain special contractile proteins — actin and myosin — that allow the tissue to contract and relax, producing movement. (पेशीय ऊतक — संकुचनशील प्रोटीन एक्टिन व मायोसिन)

 

• Muscular tissue is of three types: striated (skeletal) muscle, which is voluntary; smooth (unstriated) muscle, which is involuntary and found in the walls of internal organs; and cardiac muscle, found only in the heart, which is both striated and involuntary.

 

• Movement of the body, the pumping of the heart, and the movement of food through the alimentary canal (peristalsis) are all brought about by the contraction and relaxation of muscular tissue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nervous tissue is made of neurons and is specialised for receiving and transmitting nerve impulses; it does not itself contract.

 

• Epithelial tissue (which includes cuboidal and squamous types) forms covering and lining tissue for organs and body surfaces and functions mainly in protection, absorption and secretion.

 

• Animal tissues are broadly classified into four types: epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissue.

 

NOTE

 

• Nervous tissue (Option A): Specialised for conducting nerve impulses; its structural and functional unit is the neuron.

 

• Cuboidal epithelium tissue (Option C): A protective/absorptive tissue found in ducts of glands and kidney tubules; cube-shaped cells with no contractile function.

 

• Squamous epithelium tissue (Option D): Made of thin, flat cells; forms linings such as blood vessel walls and alveoli, mainly for diffusion and protection.

question: In which of the following groups of organisms sex determination occurs due to environmental temperature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Few reptiles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In some reptiles, such as turtles, crocodiles and certain lizards, the sex of the offspring is determined not by chromosomes but by the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are incubated — this is called Temperature-dependent Sex Determination (TSD). (तापमान-निर्भर लिंग निर्धारण — कुछ सरीसृपों में)

 

• For example, in many turtles, eggs incubated at a lower temperature develop into males, while eggs incubated at a higher temperature develop into females (in crocodiles, the pattern can be the opposite, with intermediate temperatures giving males).

 

• This is different from the genetic (chromosomal) sex determination seen in human beings, where sex is fixed at fertilisation depending on whether the sperm carries an X or a Y chromosome.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• In human beings, out of 23 pairs of chromosomes, one pair is the sex chromosome: females are XX and males are XY. The father's sperm decides the sex of the child, since the mother contributes only an X chromosome.

 

• In birds, sex is determined genetically but by a different system called the ZW system, where the female is ZW (heterogametic) and the male is ZZ — opposite to the mammalian pattern.

 

• In many fishes, sex determination can vary widely — some show chromosomal systems, and some (like certain reef fish) even show sex reversal during their lifetime, but this is not a universal temperature-based system.

 

NOTE

 

• All fishes (Option B): Sex-determination mechanisms in fish vary by species; it is not a single temperature-based rule for all fishes.

 

• All birds (Option C): Birds use the chromosomal ZW system, not environmental temperature.

 

• Human beings (Option D): Sex is determined by the XY chromosomal system, fixed at the moment of fertilisation, not by environmental temperature.

question: Which of the following statements is true?
option_1: Power and work are independent of each other.
option_2: More work done in less time means more power.
option_4: Work done does not affect power.
solution_text:
The correct answer is More work done in less time means more power.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Power is defined as the rate of doing work, i.e., Power = Work done ÷ Time taken (P = W/t). (शक्ति — कार्य करने की दर)

 

• Since power is directly proportional to work and inversely proportional to time, if the same or more work is done in less time, the power delivered is greater. This is why a powerful engine can do the same amount of work faster than a weaker one.

 

• The SI unit of power is the watt (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule/second. A larger practical unit is the kilowatt (1 kW = 1000 W), and 1 horsepower (hp) = 746 W.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Work is said to be done when a force produces a displacement in the direction of the force: W = F × s (force × displacement), and its SI unit is the joule (J).

 

• 1 joule is the work done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object through 1 metre in the direction of the force.

 

• Commercial electrical energy is measured in kilowatt-hour (kWh), popularly called a 'unit': 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

 

NOTE

 

• Power and work are independent (Option A): Incorrect — power is directly derived from work (P = W/t), so the two are directly related, not independent.

 

• Power decreases when work increases (Option C): Incorrect — for a fixed time, power actually increases as work increases; this statement wrongly reverses the relationship.

 

• Work done does not affect power (Option D): Incorrect — since P = W/t, work done directly determines power for any given time.

question: Propanone belongs to which homologous series?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ketone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Propanone (CH₃–CO–CH₃), commonly known as acetone, is the simplest member of the ketone homologous series, in which the carbonyl group (>C=O) is attached to two carbon atoms on both sides. (प्रोपेनोन/एसीटोन — कीटोन समूह)

 

• The general formula of ketones is CₙH₂ₙO, and the functional group is written as –CO– located between two carbon chains (never at the end of the chain).

 

• Acetone is a common laboratory and industrial solvent, and is also used as a nail-polish remover; it is highly volatile and inflammable.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Important homologous series and their functional groups: Alcohols (–OH), Aldehydes (–CHO), Ketones (–CO–), Carboxylic acids (–COOH), and Esters (–COO–).

 

• A homologous series is a group of organic compounds having the same general formula and similar chemical properties, with each successive member differing from the previous one by a –CH₂– unit (14 u in mass).

 

• The carbonyl group (>C=O) is common to both aldehydes and ketones, but in aldehydes it is at the end of the carbon chain (attached to at least one hydrogen), while in ketones it lies between two carbon atoms.

 

NOTE

 

• Alcohol (Option A): Characterised by the –OH group, e.g. ethanol (C₂H₅OH).

 

• Aldehyde (Option C): Characterised by the –CHO group at the end of the chain, e.g. methanal (formaldehyde, HCHO).

 

• Ester (Option D): Characterised by the –COO– group, formed from the reaction of an acid and an alcohol, e.g. ethyl acetate.

question: Which of the following statements about the Archimede's Principle is correct?
option_1: When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force that is much less than the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
option_2: When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences a downward force that is much less than the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
option_3: When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
option_4: When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences a downward force that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Archimedes' Principle states that when a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force (buoyant force or upthrust) that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the body. (आर्किमिडीज़ का सिद्धांत — उत्प्लावन बल विस्थापित द्रव के भार के बराबर)

 

• This upward force is called buoyancy or the buoyant force, and it acts through the centre of buoyancy (the centre of gravity of the displaced fluid).

 

• A body floats if its weight is less than or equal to the buoyant force it experiences when fully immersed; it sinks if its weight exceeds the maximum buoyant force possible.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Archimedes' Principle is the basis of instruments like the hydrometer (used to measure the density/specific gravity of liquids) and the lactometer (used to check the purity of milk).

 

• It also explains why ships made of iron and steel float, even though iron itself is denser than water — the hollow shape of a ship displaces a large volume of water, generating enough upthrust to balance its weight.

 

• The law of flotation follows from this principle: a floating body displaces a weight of fluid equal to its own weight.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A and B (Option A, B): Both are incorrect because the upward force is equal to, not less than, the weight of fluid displaced.

 

• Downward force equal to weight of fluid displaced (Option D): Incorrect — the buoyant force due to displaced fluid always acts upward, opposing gravity, not downward.

question: The angle between the incident ray and the emergent ray from a prism is called ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Angle of deviation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The angle of deviation is the angle between the direction of the incident ray falling on a prism and the direction of the emergent ray coming out of it, after the light has been refracted twice (once while entering and once while leaving the prism). (विचलन कोण — आपतित एवं निर्गत किरण के बीच का कोण)

 

• As white light passes through a prism, it is deviated towards the base of the prism and also split into its constituent colours (dispersion), since different colours (wavelengths) are deviated by different amounts — violet the most and red the least.

 

• For a given prism, the angle of deviation first decreases and then increases as the angle of incidence is increased, reaching a minimum value called the angle of minimum deviation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The angle of prism (A) is the angle between its two refracting surfaces, and is related to the angle of deviation and refraction by the prism formula A = r₁ + r₂.

 

• The critical angle is the angle of incidence (in a denser medium) for which the angle of refraction is 90°; beyond this angle, total internal reflection occurs.

 

• Dispersion of light through a prism produces the seven-coloured spectrum, remembered by VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red).

 

NOTE

 

• Angle of prism (Option A): The fixed angle between the two refracting surfaces of the prism, not related to the incident/emergent rays.

 

• Angle of incidence (Option B): The angle between the incident ray and the normal at the point where light enters, not the angle between incident and emergent rays.

 

• Critical angle (Option C): Relevant to total internal reflection, not to refraction through a prism.

question: Which of the following is an advantage of vegetative propagation?
option_1: Plants grown this way take longer to bear fruits.
option_2: It allows propagation of seedless plants such as banana.
option_4: All new plants are genetically different from the parent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It allows propagation of seedless plants such as banana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction in plants in which new plants are produced from vegetative parts (roots, stems, leaves) of the parent plant without the involvement of seeds. (कायिक प्रवर्धन — बीज रहित पौधों का प्रवर्धन)

 

• Its major advantage is that it allows the propagation of plants that either do not produce seeds (such as banana, seedless grapes, and seedless orange) or produce seeds that are difficult to germinate, ensuring these plants can still be grown and multiplied.

 

• Plants raised through vegetative propagation bear flowers and fruits earlier than those grown from seeds, and since the new plants come from a single parent, they are genetically identical (clones) to the parent, preserving desirable characteristics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common methods of artificial vegetative propagation include cutting (rose, sugarcane), layering (jasmine, strawberry), and grafting (mango, apple, rose).

 

• Tissue culture is a modern technique of vegetative propagation in which new plants are grown from small pieces of tissue in a nutrient medium under sterile laboratory conditions.

 

• Natural vegetative propagation occurs through structures such as the rhizome (ginger), tuber (potato), bulb (onion) and runner (grass).

 

NOTE

 

• Plants take longer to bear fruits (Option A): Incorrect — a key advantage of vegetative propagation is that plants bear flowers and fruits earlier, not later.

 

• Requires cross-pollination (Option C): Incorrect — vegetative propagation does not involve pollination or seeds at all; it is asexual.

 

• All new plants are genetically different (Option D): Incorrect — plants produced by vegetative propagation are genetically identical to the parent plant (clones).

question: The frequency of a sound wave is 250 Hz. What is its time period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.004 s.

 

GIVEN

 

• Frequency of the sound wave, f = 250 Hz.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Time period (T) and frequency (f) are related by T = 1/f.

 

• T = 1/250 = 0.004 s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For quick checks: frequency and time period are always reciprocals of each other. A frequency of 250 Hz means 250 complete oscillations occur in 1 second, so each single oscillation takes 1/250 = 0.004 s.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse frequency (measured in hertz, Hz, i.e. oscillations per second) with time period (measured in seconds, i.e. time for one oscillation) — they are inverses of one another, T = 1/f and f = 1/T.

question: What are the unwanted impurities such as soil and sand present in an ore called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gangue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The unwanted, earthy impurities such as soil, sand and rocky material present along with the ore in its naturally occurring state are called gangue. (गैंग — अयस्क में मिली अशुद्धियाँ)

 

• Before the metal can be extracted, the ore must first be concentrated (enriched) — a process in which the gangue is removed by various methods such as hydraulic washing, magnetic separation, froth flotation, and leaching, depending on the properties of the ore and the gangue.

 

• Removing gangue reduces the load on subsequent metallurgical steps such as roasting and smelting, making metal extraction more efficient and economical.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• A flux is a substance added during smelting to react with the remaining gangue in the ore and convert it into a fusible, easily removable substance called slag; e.g., limestone (CaCO₃) acts as a flux in a blast furnace.

 

• Slag is the waste product formed when flux reacts with gangue during smelting — for example, calcium silicate (CaSiO₃) slag formed in iron extraction.

 

• An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals (or a metal and a non-metal), such as brass (copper + zinc) or steel (iron + carbon), made to improve properties like hardness, strength or resistance to corrosion.

 

NOTE

 

• Slag (Option A): The waste formed when flux reacts with gangue during smelting, not the gangue itself.

 

• Alloy (Option B): A deliberately prepared homogeneous mixture of metals, unrelated to the ore's natural impurities.

 

• Flux (Option C): The substance added to the ore to remove the remaining gangue, not the gangue itself.

question: Which of the following statements about complex permanent tissue is correct?
option_1: Complex tissues are made of identical cells performing different functions.
option_2: Complex tissues are only found in animals for transporting oxygen.
option_3: Xylem and phloem are complex tissues that help in conduction and form vascular bundles.
option_4: Complex tissues consist of loosely packed parenchyma cells for storage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Xylem and phloem are complex tissues that help in conduction and form vascular bundles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Complex permanent tissues in plants are made up of more than one type of cell, all working together as a unit to perform a common function; the two main complex tissues are xylem and phloem, which together form the vascular bundles of the plant. (जटिल स्थायी ऊतक — जाइलम व फ्लोएम)

 

• Xylem conducts water and minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant, and is made up of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres; it also provides mechanical support.

 

• Phloem conducts food (prepared by photosynthesis) from the leaves to other parts of the plant, and is made up of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plant tissues are broadly divided into meristematic tissue (actively dividing) and permanent tissue (formed after growth stops), and permanent tissue is further divided into simple (one cell type, e.g. parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) and complex (more than one cell type, e.g. xylem, phloem).

 

• Xylem vessels and tracheids are dead, hollow, tube-like cells that provide a continuous channel for water transport, while sieve tubes in phloem are living cells (though they lack a nucleus at maturity) assisted by companion cells.

 

• Together, xylem and phloem form the vascular tissue system, which is essential for the transport of substances in all vascular plants.

 

NOTE

 

• Identical cells performing different functions (Option A): Incorrect — complex tissues are made of different types of cells working together for a common function, the opposite of what is stated.

 

• Only found in animals for transporting oxygen (Option B): Incorrect — complex tissues (xylem, phloem) are found in plants; oxygen transport in animals is carried out by blood, a type of connective tissue.

 

• Loosely packed parenchyma cells for storage (Option D): This describes parenchyma, which is a simple permanent tissue, not a complex one.

question: Three resistors of 4 Ω, 8 Ω, and 12 Ω are connected in series across a 12 V battery. The current in the circuit is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.5 A.

 

GIVEN

 

• Three resistors R₁ = 4 Ω, R₂ = 8 Ω, R₃ = 12 Ω connected in series; applied voltage V = 12 V.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In series, the equivalent (total) resistance is the sum of individual resistances: Rₑq = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ = 4 + 8 + 12 = 24 Ω.

 

• By Ohm's law, current I = V/R = 12/24 = 0.5 A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In series circuits, always add up all resistances first, then apply I = V/Rₑq directly — the current is the same through every resistor in a series circuit.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to treat the resistors as being in parallel; remember that in a series circuit, resistances add up directly, while in a parallel circuit, it is the reciprocals that add up.

question:
A smooth ball is resting on an ideal frictionless plane inclined on both sides. The ball is released from the left and the angle of right plane inclination is small in Case-I and zero in Case-II (flat). The ball travels _________ compared to the equally inclined case.

[Figure: a V-shaped double incline; a ball is shown released from a point on the upper part of the left slope.]
option_1: farther distance in Case-I and moves forever in Case-II
option_2: equal distance in Case-I and moves forever in Case-II
option_3: equal distance in Case-I and farther distance in Case-II
option_4: small distance in Case-I and equal distance in Case-II
solution_text:
The correct answer is farther distance in Case-I and moves forever in Case-II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This is based on Galileo's thought experiment on inertia: a ball released from a height h on a frictionless incline will always try to climb back up to the same height h on the other side, since no energy is lost to friction. (गैलीलियो का जड़त्व प्रयोग)

 

• If the equally inclined case is the reference, and in Case-I the right-side slope is made less steep (smaller angle), the ball must travel a longer distance along the slope to regain the same height h — so it goes farther than in the equally inclined case.

 

• In Case-II, the right side is made completely flat (angle = 0). Since the ball can never regain height h on a flat, frictionless surface (there is no upward slope to climb), it never stops — by Newton's first law (inertia), it keeps moving forever at constant velocity along the flat surface.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• This thought experiment historically helped establish the law of inertia: a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force — which Newton later formalised as his First Law of Motion.

 

• On a real (non-ideal) surface with friction, the ball would gradually lose energy to friction and eventually come to rest even on a flat surface — the frictionless, ideal-plane assumption is essential to this thought experiment.

 

NOTE

 

• Equal distance in Case-I and moves forever in Case-II (Option B): Incorrect for Case-I — a gentler slope means the ball must travel farther, not an equal distance, to reach the same height.

 

• Equal distance in Case-I and farther distance in Case-II (Option C): Incorrect for Case-II — on a flat surface the ball never reaches height h and moves forever, it does not simply travel 'farther'.

 

• Small distance in Case-I and equal distance in Case-II (Option D): Incorrect on both counts — a smaller incline angle means a longer (not smaller) travel distance, and a flat surface means unending motion, not an 'equal' finite distance.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about the force?
option_1: Force is a scalar quantity measured in Newton.
option_2: Force is a vector quantity measured in Joule.
option_3: Force is a vector quantity measured in Newton.
option_4: Force is a scalar quantity measured in Joule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Force is a vector quantity measured in Newton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Force is a vector quantity — it has both magnitude and direction — because the effect of a force (whether it can push, pull, accelerate or change the shape of a body) depends on the direction in which it is applied. (बल — सदिश राशि, मात्रक न्यूटन)

 

• The SI unit of force is the newton (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton; 1 newton is defined as the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a body of mass 1 kg (from F = ma).

 

• Force can change the speed, direction of motion, or shape of an object; it is calculated using Newton's second law, F = m × a.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's three laws of motion: the first law defines inertia, the second law gives F = ma, and the third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

 

• Work (W = F × s) and Energy are scalar quantities and are measured in joules (J), unlike force.

 

• The CGS unit of force is the dyne, where 1 N = 10⁵ dyne.

 

NOTE

 

• Force is scalar, measured in Newton (Option A): Incorrect — force is a vector, not a scalar, quantity.

 

• Force is vector, measured in Joule (Option B): Incorrect — the joule is the unit of work/energy, not force.

 

• Force is scalar, measured in Joule (Option D): Incorrect on both counts — force is a vector and its unit is the newton, not the joule.

question: Washing soda is prepared by heating which compound?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Washing soda (sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) is obtained by heating (recrystallising) sodium bicarbonate (baking soda, NaHCO₃). (धावन सोडा — बेकिंग सोडा को गर्म करने से)

 

• When sodium bicarbonate is heated, it decomposes to give sodium carbonate along with water and carbon dioxide: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. Recrystallising this sodium carbonate gives washing soda, which contains 10 molecules of water of crystallisation.

 

• Washing soda is used in the glass, soap and paper industries, and for removing the permanent hardness of water; it is also used domestically as a cleaning agent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda, NaHCO₃) itself is prepared industrially by the Solvay process, from sodium chloride, ammonia and carbon dioxide, and is used in baking, as an antacid, and in fire extinguishers.

 

• Bleaching powder [CaOCl₂] is prepared by the action of chlorine gas on dry slaked lime, and is used for bleaching and disinfection.

 

• Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O) is prepared by heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) at about 373 K.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcium oxide (Option B): Also called quicklime, obtained by heating limestone (CaCO₃); used to make slaked lime, not washing soda.

 

• Sodium chloride (Option C): Common salt; a raw material used in preparing sodium bicarbonate (Solvay process), but washing soda itself is made by heating baking soda, not directly from salt.

 

• Calcium carbonate (Option D): Limestone/marble; on heating, it decomposes to give calcium oxide and carbon dioxide, not washing soda.

question: What type of solution causes water to move out of a cell through the plasma membrane, making the cell shrink?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hypertonic solution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A hypertonic solution is one that has a higher concentration of solutes (lower water concentration) than the cell's cytoplasm. When a cell is placed in such a solution, water moves out of the cell by osmosis (from a region of higher water concentration to lower water concentration), causing the cell to shrink — a process called plasmolysis in plant cells. (अतिपरासारी विलयन — कोशिका का सिकुड़ना)

 

• This movement of water occurs through the semi-permeable plasma membrane, by the process of osmosis, i.e. the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential.

 

• Conversely, in a hypotonic solution (lower solute concentration than the cell), water moves into the cell, causing it to swell and possibly burst (a process called endosmosis).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• In an isotonic solution, the solute concentration outside the cell equals that inside, so there is no net movement of water, and the cell retains its normal shape and size.

 

• Plasmolysis in plant cells is used practically to preserve foods — for example, salting of pickles and jams with sugar draws water out of microbial cells (by creating a hypertonic environment), inhibiting microbial growth and preventing spoilage.

 

• Osmosis is essential for water absorption by plant roots and for maintaining the turgidity (firmness) of plant cells.

 

NOTE

 

• Isotonic solution (Option A): Causes no net movement of water in or out of the cell, since solute concentrations are equal on both sides.

 

• Dilute solution (Option C): A relative/qualitative term for low solute concentration; not a scientific term describing tonicity relative to the cell, and does not by itself specify the direction of water movement.

 

• Hypotonic solution (Option D): Causes water to move into the cell, making it swell, the opposite effect to what is described in the question.

question: Which of the following substances have a high chance of contributing to the phenomenon of biological magnification?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pesticide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Biological magnification (biomagnification) is the phenomenon in which the concentration of certain harmful, non-biodegradable chemicals, such as pesticides (e.g., DDT), increases at each successive trophic level of a food chain, becoming highest in the organisms at the top. (जैव-आवर्धन — कीटनाशकों की सांद्रता में वृद्धि)

 

• Pesticides sprayed on crops are washed into water bodies, absorbed by algae and small aquatic organisms, and then passed on and concentrated further as small fish eat these organisms, larger fish eat the small fish, and finally birds or humans eat the larger fish — this results in the highest concentration at the top of the food chain (like humans).

 

• Since such chemicals are not broken down easily (non-biodegradable) and get stored in fatty tissues, their concentration keeps rising at each step instead of getting diluted.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The classic example of biomagnification is the pesticide DDT (Dichloro-Diphenyl-Trichloroethane), whose accumulation in birds of prey caused thinning of eggshells, leading to population decline — this led to DDT being banned or restricted in many countries.

 

• Biomagnification is a key reason why the level of harmful substances is often used as an environmental indicator, and why apex predators (including humans) are most at risk from such pollutants.

 

• Biodegradable substances (like food waste, paper) can be broken down by microorganisms and therefore do not accumulate or magnify along the food chain in the same way.

 

NOTE

 

• Neem bark (Option A): A natural plant product with medicinal and pesticidal properties of its own; it is biodegradable and does not cause biomagnification.

 

• Orange peel (Option B): Biodegradable organic waste; does not accumulate in food chains.

 

• Rose petals (Option D): A biodegradable natural plant part with no role in biomagnification.

question: Why the manufacturers of chips flush chips bags with nitrogen before packing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrogen prevents rancidity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chips (and other fried/fatty foods) are packed in bags filled with nitrogen gas because nitrogen is an inert (unreactive) gas that displaces oxygen from the packet, preventing the fats and oils in the food from undergoing oxidation. (नाइट्रोजन — वसा के ऑक्सीकरण/विकृतगंधिता को रोकने हेतु)

 

• The oxidation of fats and oils leads to rancidity, in which the food develops an unpleasant smell, taste and colour, and its nutritional quality is reduced. By flushing out oxygen with nitrogen, this process is slowed down significantly, keeping the chips fresh for longer.

 

• Being inert, nitrogen also does not react with the food itself, and being under a slight positive pressure, it helps cushion the chips, reducing breakage during transport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rancidity can be prevented in general by: (i) adding antioxidants to food, (ii) storing food in air-tight containers, and (iii) storing food away from light and heat, apart from packing with an inert gas.

 

• Fats and oils undergo two main types of chemical change over time: hydrogenation (addition of hydrogen to unsaturated fats to make them saturated, as in making vanaspati ghee) and oxidation (leading to rancidity).

 

• Other common preservatives used in the food industry include salt, sugar, sodium benzoate, and vinegar, which act by inhibiting microbial growth rather than by preventing oxidation.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen prevents reduction of oil (Option A): Incorrect terminology/mechanism — the relevant chemical change nitrogen prevents is oxidation, not 'reduction'.

 

• Nitrogen acts as preservative (Option B): Too vague and not the precise mechanism being tested — its specific role is to displace oxygen and thereby prevent rancidity.

 

• Nitrogen acts as taste enhancer (Option D): Incorrect — nitrogen is inert and does not add or enhance flavour; it only protects the food from spoiling.

question: If resistors are connected in series, the total or equivalent resistance is ________.
option_1: Always less than any single resistor
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sum of individual resistances.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When resistors are connected in series, the same current flows through each of them, and the total (equivalent) resistance is the sum of the individual resistances: Rₑq = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + ... (श्रेणीक्रम — कुल प्रतिरोध व्यक्तिगत प्रतिरोधों का योग)

 

• Since resistances simply add up, the equivalent resistance in series is always greater than the greatest individual resistance in the combination — the opposite of what happens in a parallel combination.

 

• Series circuits are used where the same current is required to flow through all components, such as in a string of old-style decorative/holiday lights, where if one bulb fails, the entire circuit breaks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a parallel combination, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance equals the sum of the reciprocals of individual resistances: 1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ + ..., and the equivalent resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistor.

 

• Household electrical circuits are wired in parallel, not series, so that each appliance gets the full voltage and can operate independently, and other appliances keep working even if one fails.

 

• Ohm's Law states that V = IR, provided the temperature and other physical conditions remain constant.

 

NOTE

 

• Always less than any single resistor (Option A): This describes the equivalent resistance of a parallel, not series, combination.

 

• Product of individual resistances (Option B): Not the correct formula for either series or (in general) parallel resistors; only a shortcut used for exactly two resistors in parallel (R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂)).

 

• Reciprocal of sum of reciprocals (Option C): This describes how the equivalent resistance is found for a parallel, not series, combination.

question: The calculated formula unit mass of Na2SO4 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 142 u.

 

GIVEN

 

• Formula of the compound: Na₂SO₄ (sodium sulphate).

 

• Atomic masses: Na = 23 u, S = 32 u, O = 16 u.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Formula unit mass = (2 × atomic mass of Na) + (1 × atomic mass of S) + (4 × atomic mass of O).

 

• = (2 × 23) + (1 × 32) + (4 × 16) = 46 + 32 + 64 = 142 u.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Break the formula into its element counts first (Na₂ = 2 Na, S = 1 S, O₄ = 4 O), multiply each by its atomic mass, then simply add: 46 + 32 + 64 = 142 u.

 

NOTE

 

• For an ionic compound like Na₂SO₄, the term used is 'formula unit mass' rather than 'molecular mass', since ionic compounds exist as a network of ions rather than discrete molecules — but the calculation method (sum of atomic masses in the formula) is the same.

question: In sexually reproducing organisms, how many versions of each trait does a child inherit?
option_3: Two versions from the mother only
solution_text:
The correct answer is One version from each parent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In sexually reproducing organisms, every trait is controlled by a pair of genes called alleles, and the child inherits one allele (version) of each gene from the father and one from the mother, giving a total of two versions of every trait in the offspring. (लक्षणों की एक-एक प्रति माता व पिता से)

 

• This happens because during the formation of gametes (sperm and egg) by meiosis, each gamete carries only one copy of each gene (haploid), and when the sperm fertilises the egg, the resulting zygote gets two copies — one from each parent — restoring the diploid number.

 

• Depending on whether the two inherited versions (alleles) are the same or different, and which one is dominant, a particular trait is expressed in the offspring (as studied in Mendelian genetics).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gregor Mendel, considered the 'Father of Genetics', established the basic laws of inheritance through his experiments on pea plants (Pisum sativum).

 

• Dominant traits are those expressed even when only one copy of the allele is present (e.g., Tt shows the dominant trait), while recessive traits are expressed only when both inherited alleles are recessive (e.g., tt).

 

• Human beings have 23 pairs of chromosomes, one set of 23 inherited from the father (via sperm) and one set of 23 from the mother (via the egg).

 

NOTE

 

• One version from father only (Option A): Incorrect — a child inherits genetic material for each trait from both parents, not just the father.

 

• Two versions from the mother only (Option C): Incorrect — a child never gets both copies of a gene from a single parent under normal sexual reproduction; one comes from each parent.

 

• One version in total (Option D): Incorrect — every trait has two versions (alleles) in the offspring, one from each parent, not just one.

question: Which of the following substances is NOT an example of biodegradable substance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Plastic bags.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Biodegradable substances are those that can be broken down into simpler, harmless substances by the action of microorganisms (bacteria and fungi) in nature. Plastic bags are made of synthetic polymers that cannot be broken down easily by microorganisms, so they are non-biodegradable. (जैव-अनिम्नीकरणीय — प्लास्टिक की थैलियाँ)

 

• Plastic waste can persist in the environment for hundreds of years, causing severe pollution of soil and water bodies, and posing a threat to wildlife (e.g. through ingestion or entanglement).

 

• In contrast, spoilt food, waste paper and vegetable peels are all made of natural, organic materials that decompose readily through microbial action, returning nutrients to the soil (as in composting).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common biodegradable substances: food waste, paper, cotton and woollen cloth, wood, and other natural plant/animal products.

 

• Common non-biodegradable substances: plastics, polythene, glass, metals like aluminium, and most synthetic materials such as DDT.

 

• Excessive use of non-biodegradable materials contributes to land and water pollution; India has taken steps such as banning certain single-use plastics to curb this problem.

 

NOTE

 

• Spoilt food (Option B), Waste paper (Option C) and Vegetable peels (Option D): All of these are natural, organic substances and are readily broken down by microorganisms, making them biodegradable — hence they are not the correct answer to this 'NOT' question.

question:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option.

Statement A: Salts of strong acids and strong bases are neutral with pH 7.

Statement B: Sodium chloride is an example of a neutral salt.
option_1: Both statements A and B are correct.
option_2: Statement A is correct but B is incorrect.
option_3: Both statements A and B are incorrect.
option_4: Statement A is incorrect but B is correct.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both statements A and B are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement A is correct: Salts formed from the reaction of a strong acid and a strong base are neutral salts, having a pH equal to 7, since the acidic and basic strengths exactly cancel each other out. (उदासीन लवण — प्रबल अम्ल व प्रबल क्षार से बने)

 

• Statement B is correct: Sodium chloride (NaCl), common salt, is formed from the reaction of hydrochloric acid (a strong acid) and sodium hydroxide (a strong base): NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O, making it a classic example of a neutral salt.

 

• The nature of a salt (acidic, basic, or neutral) depends on the relative strengths of the acid and base from which it is formed, and can be summarised as: strong acid + strong base = neutral salt; strong acid + weak base = acidic salt; weak acid + strong base = basic salt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Example of an acidic salt: ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl), formed from strong acid (HCl) and weak base (NH₄OH), has a pH less than 7.

 

• Example of a basic salt: sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃), formed from weak acid (H₂CO₃) and strong base (NaOH), has a pH greater than 7.

 

• The pH scale runs from 0 to 14: values below 7 are acidic, 7 is neutral, and above 7 are basic/alkaline.

 

NOTE

 

• Statement A correct but B incorrect (Option B), Both incorrect (Option C), and A incorrect but B correct (Option D): All are ruled out because both given statements are factually accurate, as explained above.

question: What is an ion in chemistry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A charged atom or molecule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An ion is an atom or molecule that has gained or lost one or more electrons, giving it a net positive or negative electric charge. (आयन — आवेशित परमाणु या अणु)

 

• If an atom loses electrons, it becomes positively charged and is called a cation (e.g., Na⁺); if it gains electrons, it becomes negatively charged and is called an anion (e.g., Cl⁻).

 

• Ionic compounds, such as sodium chloride (NaCl), are formed by the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, and ions play an essential role in electrolysis, conduction of electricity in solutions, and many biological processes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• An atom is electrically neutral overall because it contains an equal number of protons (positive) and electrons (negative); it becomes an ion only when this balance is disturbed.

 

• A group of covalently bonded atoms that carries an overall charge is called a polyatomic ion, e.g., sulphate (SO₄²⁻), ammonium (NH₄⁺), hydroxide (OH⁻).

 

• Valency of an element is often related to the number of electrons it needs to gain or lose to form a stable ion with a complete outer shell (octet).

 

NOTE

 

• An atom with only neutrons (Option A): Not possible for any real element in its ground state — an atom always has protons in its nucleus along with neutrons; this does not describe an ion at all.

 

• A radioactive stable particle (Option C): Self-contradictory and unrelated — radioactivity refers to the spontaneous decay of unstable nuclei, not to electric charge.

 

• A neutral molecule of atom (Option D): Describes an ordinary, uncharged atom/molecule — the exact opposite of an ion, which by definition carries a net charge.

question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the principal axis of a spherical mirror?
option_2: The line passing through the focus and object
option_3: The line passing through the centre of curvature and pole
option_4: The perpendicular line drawn from the pole
solution_text:
The correct answer is The line passing through the centre of curvature and pole.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The principal axis of a spherical mirror is the straight line passing through the centre of curvature (C) and the pole (P) of the mirror; it is an imaginary line that is normal (perpendicular) to the mirror at its pole. (मुख्य अक्ष — ध्रुव व वक्रता केंद्र से गुजरने वाली रेखा)

 

• The pole (P) is the geometric centre of the mirror's reflecting surface, and the centre of curvature (C) is the centre of the hollow glass sphere of which the mirror forms a part; the radius of curvature (R) is the distance between P and C.

 

• The principal focus (F) of a spherical mirror always lies on the principal axis, exactly midway between the pole and the centre of curvature, so that R = 2f (radius of curvature = 2 × focal length).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ray diagrams for spherical mirrors are drawn using standard rules, e.g., a ray parallel to the principal axis reflects through (or appears to come from) the principal focus, and a ray passing through the centre of curvature retraces its own path after reflection.

 

• Concave mirrors (converging) are used in torches, headlights, shaving mirrors, and as reflectors in solar cookers; convex mirrors (diverging) are used as rear-view/side mirrors in vehicles because they give a wider field of view.

 

• The mirror formula relating object distance (u), image distance (v) and focal length (f) is 1/v + 1/u = 1/f.

 

NOTE

 

• The tangent at the pole (Option A): Describes the plane of the mirror's surface at the pole, not the principal axis, which is perpendicular to this tangent.

 

• The line passing through the focus and object (Option B): Not a fixed geometric feature of the mirror; the object's position varies and is unrelated to the definition of the principal axis.

 

• The perpendicular line drawn from the pole (Option D): Too vague/incomplete — infinitely many perpendiculars can be drawn from the pole; the principal axis is specifically the one passing through the centre of curvature.

question: The average age of 25 students of a class is 27 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 28 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 53.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 25 students = 27 years.

 

• Average age of 26 people (25 students + teacher) = 28 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total age of 25 students = 25 × 27 = 675 years.

 

• Total age of 26 people = 26 × 28 = 728 years.

 

• Age of teacher = 728 − 675 = 53 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Teacher's age = old average + (number of students) × (increase in average) = 27 + 25 × (28 − 27) = 27 + 25 = 52... check: actually use: New person's value = new average + n(old)×(change) = 28 + 25×1 = 53. So teacher's age = new average + old count × increase = 28 + 25 × 1 = 53.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever a new member changes the average of a group, use: New member's value = New average + (old number of members) × (change in average), taking the change as positive if the average increased.

question: If 20% of a number is added to 72, then the result is the same number. 60% of the same number is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 54.

 

GIVEN

 

• 20% of a number, added to 72, gives back the same number.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number be x. Then 72 + 0.20x = x.

 

• 72 = x − 0.20x = 0.80x ⇒ x = 72/0.80 = 90.

 

• 60% of 90 = 0.60 × 90 = 54.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 72 represents 80% of the number (since the remaining 20% makes up the number itself), so the number = 72 × (100/80) = 90; then 60% of 90 = 54.

 

NOTE

 

• Convert 'x added to y% of x equals x' into 'y is the complement of x's percentage' — here 72 corresponds to (100 − 20)% = 80% of the number.

question: Amit and Deeksha together invested ₹46,800 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹8,700, Amit's share was ₹2,900. What was the investment of Amit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹15,600.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total investment (Amit + Deeksha) = ₹46,800.

 

• Total profit = ₹8,700, of which Amit's share = ₹2,900.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In a partnership (same time period for both), profit share is directly proportional to investment.

 

• Deeksha's profit share = 8,700 − 2,900 = ₹5,800.

 

• Ratio of profits Amit : Deeksha = 2,900 : 5,800 = 1 : 2, so the investment ratio is also 1 : 2 (total 3 parts).

 

• Amit's investment = (1/3) × 46,800 = ₹15,600.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since profit ratio = investment ratio for the same time period, just simplify the given profit shares (2,900 : 5,800 = 1 : 2) and apply that ratio directly to the total investment.

 

NOTE

 

• This shortcut (profit ratio = investment ratio) works only when all partners invest for the same length of time; if not, you must use capital × time for each partner.

question: The income of Raman is ₹68,500. He saves 22.5% of his income. If his income increases by 14% and expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. decrease by ₹11,645.

 

GIVEN

 

• Income = ₹68,500; savings = 22.5% of income; income increases by 14%, expenditure increases by 40%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Original savings = 22.5% of 68,500 = 0.225 × 68,500 = ₹15,412.50.

 

• Original expenditure = income − savings = 68,500 − 15,412.50 = ₹53,087.50.

 

• New income = 68,500 × 1.14 = ₹78,090.

 

• New expenditure = 53,087.50 × 1.40 = ₹74,322.50.

 

• New savings = new income − new expenditure = 78,090 − 74,322.50 = ₹3,767.50.

 

• Change in savings = 3,767.50 − 15,412.50 = −₹11,645, i.e. a decrease of ₹11,645.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always compute the actual old and new savings figures directly (savings = income − expenditure) rather than trying to combine percentage changes of income and expenditure directly, since savings is a small difference of two large, differently-changing quantities.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to apply percentage change formulas meant for profit/loss directly to 'savings' — but savings is not simply income minus a percentage of income; it is the actual difference between two separately changing quantities, so compute each precisely.

question: A flight travels a distance of 1,200 km in 3 hours. What is the speed of the flight?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 400 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Distance = 1,200 km; Time = 3 hours.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 1,200 ÷ 3 = 400 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a direct distance/time question, just divide: 1200/3 = 400 — no intermediate conversion needed since both are already in km and hours.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check the units given match the units asked; here both distance (km) and time (hr) directly give speed in km/hr without conversion.

question: If the price of a product is first increased by 18% and then decreased by 22%. Find the percentage change in the price (correct to two places of decimals).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Decreased by 7.96%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Price is first increased by 18%, then decreased by 22%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the original price = 100. After +18%: 100 × 1.18 = 118.

 

• After −22% on 118: 118 × 0.78 = 92.04.

 

• Net change = 92.04 − 100 = −7.96, i.e. a decrease of 7.96%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net % change for two successive percentage changes a% and b% = a + b + (ab/100). Here a = +18, b = −22: net = 18 − 22 + (18 × −22)/100 = −4 − 3.96 = −7.96% (a decrease of 7.96%).

 

NOTE

 

• Never simply subtract 22 − 18 = 4%; successive percentage changes must be combined using the formula a + b + ab/100, because the second change is applied to the already-changed value, not the original.

question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7% per annum, respectively. Keshav borrowed an amount of ₹4,80,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Keshav after 2 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹33,600.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal borrowed from each bank = ₹4,80,000; Rate A = 3.5% p.a., Rate B = 7% p.a.; Time = 2 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Simple Interest = (P × R × T)/100.

 

• SI from Bank A = (4,80,000 × 3.5 × 2)/100 = ₹33,600.

 

• SI from Bank B = (4,80,000 × 7 × 2)/100 = ₹67,200.

 

• Positive difference = 67,200 − 33,600 = ₹33,600.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since the principal and time are the same for both banks, the difference in simple interest is directly proportional to the difference in rates: SI difference = P × (R₂ − R₁) × T/100 = 4,80,000 × (7 − 3.5) × 2/100 = 4,80,000 × 3.5 × 2/100 = ₹33,600.

 

NOTE

 

• When principal and time are identical, you don't need to calculate both interests separately — just apply the rate difference directly to save time.

question: The marked price of a bed is ₹744, which is 36% above the cost price. If the profit percentage is 20%, find the discount percentage (rounded off to two decimal places).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 11.76%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = ₹744, which is 36% above Cost Price (CP); required profit = 20%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• CP = MP ÷ 1.36 = 744 ÷ 1.36 = ₹547.0588... .

 

• Selling Price (SP) for 20% profit = CP × 1.20 = 547.0588 × 1.20 = ₹656.4706.

 

• Discount = MP − SP = 744 − 656.4706 = ₹87.5294.

 

• Discount % = (Discount/MP) × 100 = (87.5294/744) × 100 ≈ 11.76%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take CP = 100. Then MP = 136. Required SP (20% profit) = 120. Discount = 136 − 120 = 16 on MP of 136. Discount % = (16/136) × 100 = 11.76% — this ratio is independent of the actual ₹744 value, so you never need the real numbers at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Discount is always calculated as a percentage of the Marked Price, and profit as a percentage of the Cost Price — mixing up the bases is the most common error in such questions.

question: Simplify: (2³ × 3⁻² × 5⁴)/(6⁻¹ × 10²).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 2² × 3⁻¹ × 5².

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: (2³ × 3⁻² × 5⁴) ÷ (6⁻¹ × 10²).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Break the denominator into prime factors: 6⁻¹ = (2 × 3)⁻¹ = 2⁻¹ × 3⁻¹, and 10² = (2 × 5)² = 2² × 5².

 

• So denominator = 2⁻¹ × 3⁻¹ × 2² × 5² = 2^(−1+2) × 3⁻¹ × 5² = 2¹ × 3⁻¹ × 5².

 

• Now divide: (2³ × 3⁻² × 5⁴) ÷ (2¹ × 3⁻¹ × 5²) = 2^(3−1) × 3^(−2−(−1)) × 5^(4−2) = 2² × 3⁻¹ × 5².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always resolve composite bases (6, 10) into their prime factors (2, 3, 5) first, then subtract exponents of like bases directly — this avoids errors in combining unlike bases.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the law of exponents: aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = a^(m−n), applied separately to each prime base after full factorisation.

question: The ratio of the price per unit of lemon chocolate to that of strawberry chocolate is 22 : 6, and a family consumes them in the ratio 14 : 23 by quantity. Determine the ratio of the expenditure on strawberry chocolate to that on lemon chocolate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 69 : 154.

 

GIVEN

 

• Price ratio, lemon : strawberry = 22 : 6 = 11 : 3.

 

• Quantity consumed ratio, lemon : strawberry = 14 : 23.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Expenditure = Price × Quantity.

 

• Expenditure on lemon chocolate ∝ 11 × 14 = 154.

 

• Expenditure on strawberry chocolate ∝ 3 × 23 = 69.

 

• Required ratio (strawberry : lemon) = 69 : 154.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Simplify the price ratio first (22:6 → 11:3) to keep the numbers small, then simply cross-multiply price × quantity for each item to get the expenditure ratio directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always read carefully which ratio is asked (strawberry : lemon here, not lemon : strawberry) — reversing the order is the most common slip in such questions.

question:
Arrange the following schemes in the ascending order of their discounts.

A. Buy 3 get 2 free.

B. A single discount of 65%.

C. Two successive discounts of 31% and 40%.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. A, C, B.

 

GIVEN

 

• Scheme A: Buy 3, get 2 free. Scheme B: single discount of 65%. Scheme C: successive discounts of 31% and 40%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scheme A: pay for 3 items, get 5 items in total, so the discount = (5 − 3)/5 × 100 = 2/5 × 100 = 40%.

 

• Scheme B: a flat 65% discount.

 

• Scheme C: combine 31% and 40% using the successive-discount formula: net discount = 31 + 40 − (31 × 40)/100 = 71 − 12.4 = 58.6%.

 

• Comparing: A (40%) < C (58.6%) < B (65%), so the ascending order is A, C, B.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For successive discounts a% and b%, net discount = a + b − ab/100 (always less than a simple sum, since the second discount applies to an already-reduced price).

 

NOTE

 

• 'Buy 3 get 2 free' effectively means pay for 3 out of 5, so the discount fraction is (free items)/(total items received), not (free items)/(items paid for) — a common point of confusion.

question: A solid sphere of radius 7 cm is coated with a layer of paint that increases its radius to 7.5 cm, find the volume of the painted layer. (Use π = 22/7 and round off your answer to the nearest integer)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 331 cm³.

 

GIVEN

 

• Inner radius (sphere) r = 7 cm; outer radius (sphere + paint) R = 7.5 cm; π = 22/7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of painted layer = Volume of outer sphere − Volume of inner sphere = (4/3)π(R³ − r³).

 

• R³ = 7.5³ = 421.875; r³ = 7³ = 343. So R³ − r³ = 421.875 − 343 = 78.875.

 

• Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 78.875 = (4 × 22 × 78.875)/(3 × 7) = 6941/21 ≈ 330.52 cm³.

 

• Rounded to the nearest integer: 331 cm³.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a thin shell/layer between two spheres, always use the difference of cubes (R³ − r³) inside the sphere volume formula directly, rather than calculating and subtracting two large volumes separately — it keeps the numbers smaller and reduces rounding error.

 

NOTE

 

• Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³ — remember this is different from the surface area formula (4πr²); mixing the two up is a common mistake.

question: If 30 workers earn ₹4140 in 4 days, how much (in ₹) will 55 workers earn in 10 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹18,975.

 

GIVEN

 

• 30 workers earn ₹4,140 in 4 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Earning of 1 worker in 1 day = 4,140 ÷ (30 × 4) = 4,140 ÷ 120 = ₹34.5.

 

• Earning of 55 workers in 10 days = 34.5 × 55 × 10 = 34.5 × 550 = ₹18,975.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use the direct proportion method: New earning = Old earning × (new workers/old workers) × (new days/old days) = 4,140 × (55/30) × (10/4) = 4,140 × 55 × 10/(30 × 4) = 18,975.

 

NOTE

 

• Earnings/work done is directly proportional to both the number of workers and the number of days — always set up the ratio for both factors together rather than one at a time to avoid errors.

question: Five years ago, the ratio of the ages of two buildings was 7 : 2. Five years hence, the ratio will be 3 : 1. What is the present age of the newer building?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 45 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• 5 years ago, ratio of ages of the two buildings = 7 : 2.

 

• 5 years hence (from now), ratio of ages = 3 : 1.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the ages 5 years ago be 7x and 2x. Then 5 years hence, ages will be (7x + 10) and (2x + 10).

 

• (7x + 10)/(2x + 10) = 3/1 ⇒ 7x + 10 = 6x + 30 ⇒ x = 20.

 

• Age of the newer (smaller) building 5 years ago = 2x = 40 years, so its present age = 40 + 5 = 45 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up the two ratio conditions directly as equations in a single variable x (representing the common multiplying factor 5 years ago) — this avoids handling four unknowns and reduces the problem to one linear equation.

 

NOTE

 

• Be careful to add the correct number of years on both sides when moving from '5 years ago' all the way to '5 years hence' — that is a total shift of 10 years from the 'ago' reference point.

question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 2, 5 and 20 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do thrice the same work, working together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 4 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• A can finish the work in 2 days, B in 5 days, C in 20 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• One day's work: A = 1/2, B = 1/5, C = 1/20.

 

• Combined one day's work = 1/2 + 1/5 + 1/20 = 10/20 + 4/20 + 1/20 = 15/20 = 3/4.

 

• Time to finish 1 work together = 1 ÷ (3/4) = 4/3 days.

 

• Time to finish thrice the work = 3 × 4/3 = 4 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take total work (LCM of 2, 5, 20) = 20 units. Efficiencies: A = 10, B = 4, C = 1 unit/day, combined = 15 units/day. Thrice the work = 60 units. Time = 60/15 = 4 days.

 

NOTE

 

• Using LCM-based 'units of work' (efficiency method) instead of fractions is usually faster and less error-prone for combined work problems.

question: A class of 69 students took a Physics test. 17 students had an average score of 94. The other students had an average score of 84. What is the average score (rounded off to one decimal place) of the whole class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 86.5.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total students = 69; 17 students averaged 94; remaining (69 − 17 = 52) students averaged 84.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total marks of first group = 17 × 94 = 1,598.

 

• Total marks of second group = 52 × 84 = 4,368.

 

• Total marks of whole class = 1,598 + 4,368 = 5,966.

 

• Average of whole class = 5,966 ÷ 69 = 86.4637... ≈ 86.5 (to one decimal place).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use the weighted average (alligation) idea: overall average lies between 84 and 94, closer to 84 since more students (52) scored 84 than scored 94 (17) — a quick sanity check that the answer should be well below the midpoint (89), consistent with 86.5.

 

NOTE

 

• Always find the total marks of each subgroup first (average × count) before combining, rather than averaging the two averages directly — the groups here are of different sizes, so a simple average of 94 and 84 would be wrong.

question: A number when multiplied by 3 and then added to 8, results in 29. What is the number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 7.

 

GIVEN

 

• A number, multiplied by 3 and then added to 8, gives 29.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number be x. Then 3x + 8 = 29.

 

• 3x = 29 − 8 = 21 ⇒ x = 21/3 = 7.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Reverse the operations from the result: subtract 8 from 29 to undo the addition (29 − 8 = 21), then divide by 3 to undo the multiplication (21 ÷ 3 = 7).

 

NOTE

 

• For such 'number puzzle' questions, always translate the words into an equation step by step in the order given, then solve by reversing the operations from the final result.

question: A hollow metallic sphere with an external radius of 10 cm and an internal radius of 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid cone with a base radius of 8 cm. What is the height of the cone? (Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 49 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Hollow sphere: external radius R = 10 cm, internal radius r = 6 cm.

 

• This is melted and recast into a solid cone of base radius 8 cm; π = 22/7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of hollow sphere = (4/3)π(R³ − r³) = (4/3)π(1000 − 216) = (4/3)π × 784.

 

• Volume of cone = (1/3)π(8)²h = (1/3)π × 64 × h.

 

• Since the metal is recast (volume conserved): (4/3)π × 784 = (1/3)π × 64 × h.

 

• Cancel (1/3)π from both sides: 4 × 784 = 64h ⇒ 3,136 = 64h ⇒ h = 3,136/64 = 49 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since volume is conserved in melting/recasting, always equate the two volume formulas directly and cancel common factors (like π and 1/3) immediately, rather than computing each volume fully with π = 22/7 first — this avoids unnecessary decimal calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Volume of hollow sphere/shell = (4/3)π(R³ − r³) — remember to use the difference of cubes, not the difference of squares, since it is a volume (3-D) quantity.

question: If x² + 1/x² = 79, then a possible value of (x + 1/x) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 9.

 

GIVEN

 

• x² + 1/x² = 79.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the identity: (x + 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² + 2.

 

• (x + 1/x)² = 79 + 2 = 81.

 

• x + 1/x = √81 = 9.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever x² + 1/x² is given, add 2 to it and take the square root to get x + 1/x directly: √(79 + 2) = √81 = 9 — no need to solve for x itself.

 

NOTE

 

• Similarly, if x² + 1/x² is given and (x − 1/x) is asked, subtract 2 instead of adding: (x − 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² − 2.

question: A train of length 299 m takes 12 seconds to pass another train 101 m long coming from the opposite direction. If the speed of the first train is 71 km/hr, then find the speed of the second train.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 49 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train 1 length = 299 m, Train 2 length = 101 m; they cross each other (opposite direction) in 12 s; speed of Train 1 = 71 km/hr.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total distance to be covered while crossing = sum of both lengths = 299 + 101 = 400 m.

 

• Relative speed = distance/time = 400/12 = 100/3 m/s.

 

• Convert to km/hr: (100/3) × (18/5) = 1800/15 = 120 km/hr.

 

• For trains moving in opposite directions, relative speed = sum of individual speeds: 120 = 71 + speed of Train 2.

 

• Speed of Train 2 = 120 − 71 = 49 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Remember: m/s × 18/5 = km/hr, and km/hr × 5/18 = m/s. For crossing questions, always use (sum of lengths)/(time) to get relative speed first.

 

NOTE

 

• Opposite directions ⇒ relative speed = sum of speeds; same direction ⇒ relative speed = difference of speeds. Mixing these up is the most common error in train-crossing problems.

question: A camp has provisions for 42 pupils for 12 days. In how many days will the same provisions finish off if the strength of the camp is increased to 63 pupils?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 8 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• Provisions last 42 pupils for 12 days; strength increased to 63 pupils.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total provisions (in pupil-days) = 42 × 12 = 504.

 

• Number of days for 63 pupils = 504 ÷ 63 = 8 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use inverse proportion directly: New days = Old days × (Old pupils/New pupils) = 12 × (42/63) = 12 × (2/3) = 8 days.

 

NOTE

 

• More people consuming the same fixed provisions means fewer days will last — always check that the answer decreases when the number of people increases (and vice versa) as a sanity check.

question: P is any point inside the rectangle ABCD. If PA = 86 cm, PB = 49 cm and PC = 79 cm, then the length of PD (in cm) is equal to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 106 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• P is any point inside rectangle ABCD, with PA = 86 cm, PB = 49 cm, PC = 79 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For any point P inside a rectangle ABCD (with A, B, C, D taken in order), the property holds: PA² + PC² = PB² + PD².

 

• PA² = 86² = 7,396; PC² = 79² = 6,241; sum = 7,396 + 6,241 = 13,637.

 

• PB² = 49² = 2,401.

 

• PD² = 13,637 − 2,401 = 11,236 ⇒ PD = √11,236 = 106 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the rectangle-point property: PA² + PC² = PB² + PD² (opposite vertex pairs) — this converts a seemingly complex geometry question into a one-line algebraic equation.

 

NOTE

 

• This property applies specifically to a point inside a rectangle and its two pairs of opposite vertices (A,C and B,D) — the vertices must be taken in the correct cyclic order (A, B, C, D).

question: A baker sells 100 cupcakes and earns a profit equal to the selling price of 20 cupcakes. What is his profit percentage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 25%.

 

GIVEN

 

• 100 cupcakes are sold; profit earned = selling price of 20 cupcakes.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the selling price of 1 cupcake = s. Total SP (of 100 cupcakes) = 100s.

 

• Profit = SP of 20 cupcakes = 20s.

 

• Cost Price = SP − Profit = 100s − 20s = 80s.

 

• Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (20s/80s) × 100 = 25%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Profit % = (profit units)/(cost-price units) × 100 = 20/(100 − 20) × 100 = 20/80 × 100 = 25% — directly using the number of 'cupcakes-worth' as units instead of introducing a price variable.

 

NOTE

 

• Always express profit percentage as a fraction of the Cost Price, not the Selling Price — a very common trap in such 'profit equals SP of some units' questions.

question: Find the value of sin15°/cos75° + cos78°/sin12° − 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: sin15°/cos75° + cos78°/sin12° − 1.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the co-function identity: sin θ = cos(90° − θ) and cos θ = sin(90° − θ).

 

• sin15° = cos(90° − 15°) = cos75°, so sin15°/cos75° = cos75°/cos75° = 1.

 

• cos78° = sin(90° − 78°) = sin12°, so cos78°/sin12° = sin12°/sin12° = 1.

 

• Expression = 1 + 1 − 1 = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever you see two angles that add up to 90° (like 15° & 75°, or 78° & 12°) in a sin/cos ratio, the ratio simplifies to exactly 1 using sin θ = cos(90° − θ) — spot this pattern immediately instead of using a calculator/table.

 

NOTE

 

• Key co-function identities: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, cos(90° − θ) = sin θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ — these are extremely useful for simplifying trigonometric expressions quickly.

question: A cistern of dimensions 100 cm × 80 cm × 120 cm is fitted with an inlet pipe and an outlet pipe. The inlet pipe pours in 2000 cm³ of water per minute and the outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 3 hours and 20 minutes. If the tank is full and both pipes are open, then how many hours will it take to empty the cistern?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 5 5/7 hours.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cistern dimensions: 100 cm × 80 cm × 120 cm; inlet pipe fills at 2,000 cm³/min; outlet pipe alone empties the full tank in 3 hr 20 min.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of cistern = 100 × 80 × 120 = 9,60,000 cm³.

 

• Outlet time = 3 hr 20 min = 200 minutes, so outlet rate = 9,60,000 ÷ 200 = 4,800 cm³/min.

 

• With both pipes open, net emptying rate = outlet rate − inlet rate = 4,800 − 2,000 = 2,800 cm³/min.

 

• Time to empty full cistern = 9,60,000 ÷ 2,800 = 342.857... minutes = 342 6/7 minutes.

 

• Converting to hours: 342.857/60 = 5.7142... hours = 5 5/7 hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert everything to a single rate (cm³/min) first, find the net emptying rate by subtracting the inlet rate from the outlet rate, then divide the total volume by this net rate — always keep units consistent throughout (here, cm³ and minutes) before converting the final answer to hours.

 

NOTE

 

• When inlet and outlet pipes work simultaneously in opposite senses (one fills, one empties), their rates subtract, not add; the net rate determines whether the tank ultimately fills or empties.

question: P, Q, R, S, T and U are sitting in a row facing the north. S is sitting to the immediate left of Q. P is sitting to the immediate right of Q. U is sitting to the immediate right of P and immediate left of T. S and R are sitting at the ends of the line not necessarily in the same order. Who is sitting to the immediate right of T?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. R.

 

GIVEN

 

• S is immediate left of Q; P is immediate right of Q; U is immediate right of P and immediate left of T; S and R sit at the two ends (order not fixed).

 

SOLUTION

 

• S immediate left of Q, and P immediate right of Q, gives the block: S - Q - P (three consecutive seats).

 

• U is immediate right of P and immediate left of T, giving: P - U - T (three consecutive seats), which extends the block to: S - Q - P - U - T (five consecutive people).

 

• This 5-person block occupies 5 of the 6 seats; the 6th person is R. Since S is already at the left edge of this block and S must be at one end of the whole row, the block occupies positions 1 to 5, and R takes position 6 (the right end) — satisfying 'S and R at the ends'.

 

• Final seating (left to right): S, Q, P, U, T, R.

 

• The person immediately to the right of T (position 5) is at position 6, which is R.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain together the 'immediate left/right' clues first to build one continuous block (S-Q-P-U-T), then use the 'ends' condition only at the end to fix the position of the one remaining person.

 

NOTE

 

• Always build the largest possible connected block from the direct 'immediate left/right' clues before using looser conditions (like 'sits at the ends') — this reduces the number of cases to check.

question:
Aditi starts from Point A and drives 10 km towards the west. She then takes a left turn, drives 8 km, turns right and drives 5 km. She then takes a left turn and drives 8 km. She then takes a left turn and drives 15 km. She takes a final right turn, drives 4 km and stops at Point D. How far (shortest distance) and in which direction is Point D with respect from Point A?

(All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 20 km towards south.

 

GIVEN

 

• Starting at A, take east as +x and north as +y. Path: 10 km west; left turn, 8 km; right turn, 5 km; left turn, 8 km; left turn, 15 km; right turn, 4 km, stop at D.

 

SOLUTION

 

• A = (0, 0). Drive 10 km west (facing West): reach (−10, 0).

 

• Left turn from West → facing South. Drive 8 km south: reach (−10, −8).

 

• Right turn from South → facing West. Drive 5 km west: reach (−15, −8).

 

• Left turn from West → facing South. Drive 8 km south: reach (−15, −16).

 

• Left turn from South → facing East. Drive 15 km east: reach (0, −16).

 

• Right turn from East → facing South. Drive 4 km south: reach (0, −20). This is Point D.

 

• D = (0, −20) is directly south of A = (0, 0), at a shortest distance of 20 km, direction south.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the net east-west and net north-south displacement as running totals; ignore intermediate turns except to know the new facing direction — here the east-west displacement cancelled out exactly to 0, leaving a pure south displacement of 20 km.

 

NOTE

 

• Memorise the turning rule: facing any direction, a right turn moves you one step clockwise (N→E→S→W→N) and a left turn moves you one step anticlockwise (N→W→S→E→N).

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some books are novels.

All novels are stories.

Conclusions:

(I): Some stories are books.

(II): No books are stories.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: Some books are novels (particular affirmative, I-type).

 

• Statement 2: All novels are stories (universal affirmative, A-type).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Combining 'Some books are novels' and 'All novels are stories' (an I + A combination with the middle term 'novels' distributed in the second premise) gives the valid conclusion: Some books are stories.

 

• Conclusion (I), 'Some stories are books', is simply the converse of 'Some books are stories' — and conversion of a particular affirmative (I-type) statement is always valid. So Conclusion (I) follows.

 

• Conclusion (II), 'No books are stories', directly contradicts the valid derived conclusion 'Some books are stories', so it cannot follow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw a quick Venn diagram: a small circle for 'novels' completely inside 'stories', with 'books' overlapping 'novels'. This immediately shows that the books-novels overlap must also fall inside 'stories', proving 'Some books are stories' (and hence its converse) true, while ruling out 'No books are stories'.

 

NOTE

 

• A particular statement ('Some A are B') can always be validly converted to ('Some B are A') — this conversion rule is frequently the key to solving syllogism questions quickly.

question:
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) in the following series to make it logically complete?

IDR LGQ OJP RMO ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. UPN.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: IDR, LGQ, OJP, RMO, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Split each cluster into its 1st, 2nd and 3rd letters and track each position separately (using A=1, B=2, ..., Z=26).
