• 1st letters: I(9), L(12), O(15), R(18) → increasing by 3 each time → next = 18 + 3 = 21 = U.

 

• 2nd letters: D(4), G(7), J(10), M(13) → increasing by 3 each time → next = 13 + 3 = 16 = P.

 

• 3rd letters: R(18), Q(17), P(16), O(15) → decreasing by 1 each time → next = 15 − 1 = 14 = N.

 

• Missing cluster = U, P, N = UPN.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For multi-letter cluster series, always separate the clusters column-wise (1st letters together, 2nd letters together, etc.) and find the pattern in each column independently — mixing the letters together makes the pattern much harder to spot.

 

NOTE

 

• Convert letters to their alphabet positions (A=1...Z=26) before checking for arithmetic patterns; this is far easier than trying to spot patterns in the letters directly.

question:
In a certain code language,

'A ? B' means 'A is the daughter of B',

'A = B' means 'A is the son of B',

'A @ B' means 'A is the father of B' and

'A √ B' means 'A is the sister of B'.

How is C related to L if 'C ? D = E @ F √ L'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Brother's daughter.

 

GIVEN

 

• Coded expression: C ? D = E @ F √ L, with '?' = daughter of, '=' = son of, '@' = father of, '√' = sister of.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'C ? D' → C is the daughter of D.

 

• 'D = E' → D is the son of E.

 

• 'E @ F' → E is the father of F.

 

• 'F √ L' → F is the sister of L.

 

• Since F is the sister of L, they share the same parents; so E (father of F) is also the father of L.

 

• D is the son of E, so D is a son of the same parents as F and L, making D the brother of L.

 

• C is the daughter of D, so from L's point of view, C is the daughter of L's brother D, i.e., C is L's brother's daughter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw a simple family tree from the innermost relation outward (start from 'F √ L' and 'E @ F' to fix the parent-child-sibling structure), then attach 'D = E' and 'C ? D' at the end — building the tree step by step avoids confusion in long coded-relation chains.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever two people share the same father (or mother), they are automatically siblings of each other — this is the key link that connects D and L as brother-sister in this chain.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one that follows the same logic.

RAGE - ARGE - EARG

QUIZ - UQIZ - ZUQI
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. HERD - EHRD - DEHR.

 

GIVEN

 

• Example 1: RAGE → ARGE → EARG. Example 2: QUIZ → UQIZ → ZUQI.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word 1 → word 2): swap the 1st and 2nd letters. RAGE (R,A,G,E) → ARGE (A,R,G,E) ✓; QUIZ (Q,U,I,Z) → UQIZ (U,Q,I,Z) ✓.

 

• Step 2 (word 2 → word 3): move the last letter to the front (a one-place right rotation of the whole word), keeping the other three letters in the same order. ARGE (A,R,G,E) → move E to front → E,A,R,G = EARG ✓; UQIZ (U,Q,I,Z) → move Z to front → Z,U,Q,I = ZUQI ✓.

 

• Apply both confirmed rules to Option D: HERD (H,E,R,D) → swap 1st & 2nd letters → EHRD (E,H,R,D) ✓ matches the given middle term.

 

• EHRD (E,H,R,D) → move the last letter (D) to the front → D,E,H,R = DEHR ✓ matches the given third term exactly.

 

• Since HERD - EHRD - DEHR follows both steps of the confirmed pattern exactly, it is the correct triad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First check ONLY the word1 → word2 transition in each option — it must be a simple swap of the first two letters; this alone eliminates most wrong options quickly. Then confirm word2 → word3 by checking whether the last letter of word 2 has simply moved to the front to form word 3.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Move the last letter to the front' is a common letter-shuffling rule in such triad questions — always test simple rotations (shifting letters left or right by one place) before assuming a more complex transformation is at work.

question:
O, P, Q, R, W, X and Y are sitting in a straight line facing north.

Only three people sit to the left of P. Only R sits to the right of Q. Only three people sit between Q and O. X sits at some place to the left of Y but at some place to the right of W.

How many people sit between W and Y?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people O, P, Q, R, W, X, Y in a line, positions 1 (leftmost) to 7 (rightmost).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Only three people sit to the left of P ⇒ P is at position 4.

 

• Only R sits to the right of Q ⇒ Q is second-last and R is last: Q at position 6, R at position 7.

 

• Only three people sit between Q and O ⇒ |position(O) − 6| − 1 = 3 ⇒ position(O) = 2 (since position 10 is invalid) ⇒ O at position 2.

 

• Remaining positions 1, 3, 5 are for W, X, Y. Given W < X < Y (X left of Y, right of W): W = 1, X = 3, Y = 5.

 

• Final order: W(1), O(2), X(3), P(4), Y(5), Q(6), R(7).

 

• Number of people between W(1) and Y(5) = those at positions 2, 3, 4 = O, X, P = three people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the absolute positions given directly first (P=4, Q=6, R=7, O=2), since these come from precise 'only N to the left/right' clues — only then work out the relative order of the remaining people using the looser left-right clue.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only N people sit to the left of X' fixes X's position directly as (N+1) from the left in a row of known total size — a very reliable starting clue in linear arrangement puzzles.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

5 8 14 23 35 50 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 68.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 5, 8, 14, 23, 35, 50, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the first differences: 8−5=3, 14−8=6, 23−14=9, 35−23=12, 50−35=15.

 

• The differences themselves form an arithmetic progression increasing by 3 each time: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, so the next difference = 15 + 3 = 18.

 

• Next term = 50 + 18 = 68.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a number series doesn't have a constant difference, always take the difference of the differences — a constant second difference (here, always +3) confirms the series follows a quadratic pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• Series with a constant second difference can also be written as a quadratic formula in n, but for exam purposes, simply extending the difference pattern one more step (as done here) is faster.

question:
If + means -, - means x, x means ÷, ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

12 - 15 ÷ 143 + 98 x 7 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 309.

 

GIVEN

 

• Symbol substitution: + means −, − means ×, × means ÷, ÷ means +.

 

• Expression: 12 − 15 ÷ 143 + 98 × 7 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace each symbol with its actual meaning: '−' becomes '×', '÷' becomes '+', '+' becomes '−', '×' becomes '÷'.

 

• Rewritten expression: 12 × 15 + 143 − 98 ÷ 7.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 98 ÷ 7 = 14; 12 × 15 = 180.

 

• Now compute: 180 + 143 − 14 = 323 − 14 = 309.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First rewrite the entire expression with the correct (swapped) symbols on paper before calculating anything — attempting to calculate and substitute symbols simultaneously is the most common source of errors in such questions.

 

NOTE

 

• After substituting the symbols, always apply the standard order of operations (BODMAS/VBODMAS) to the rewritten expression, exactly as you would for a normal arithmetic expression.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(6, 72, 12)

(5, 60, 12)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. (3, 36, 12).

 

GIVEN

 

• Pattern sets: (6, 72, 12) and (5, 60, 12).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the relationship: 6 × 12 = 72 ✓ (matches middle number); 5 × 12 = 60 ✓ (matches middle number). So the rule is: 1st number × 3rd number = 2nd number, with the 3rd number fixed at 12 in both given sets.

 

• Test option C: (3, 36, 12) → 3 × 12 = 36 ✓. This matches the pattern exactly, using the same third number (12) as both given examples.

 

• Testing the other options against 1st × 3rd = 2nd: (A) 7×12=84≠82; (B) 4×13=52≠48; (D) 2×14=28≠24 — none of these satisfy the rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With two given example sets sharing a common third number (here, both have 12), test the simplest relationship first — multiplication of the 1st and 3rd numbers to get the 2nd — since it is the most common such pattern in these questions.

 

NOTE

 

• The question's note insists numbers must be used as whole numbers (e.g. treat '72' as seventy-two, not digits '7' and '2' separately) — always re-read such notes carefully as they restrict the type of operation allowed.

question:
A, B, C, D, W, X and Y are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table.

Only four people sit between B and A when counted from the right of B. B sits third to the left of X. W sits third to the left of Y. C is an immediate neighbour of both A and X.

How many people sit between D and C when counted from the right of D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people around a circular table, facing the centre; positions numbered 1 to 7 clockwise. Take clockwise as 'right' and anticlockwise as 'left' (as viewed for people facing the centre).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let B be at position 1. 'Only four people between B and A, counted from the right of B' means moving clockwise from B, 4 people come before reaching A ⇒ A is at position 6.

 

• 'B sits third to the left of X' means X is three positions clockwise from B ⇒ X is at position 4.

 

• 'C is an immediate neighbour of both A(6) and X(4)': neighbours of A are positions 5,7; neighbours of X are positions 3,5 — the common position is 5, so C is at position 5.

 

• Remaining positions 2, 3, 7 are for D, W, Y, with 'W third to the left of Y' meaning Y is three positions clockwise from W. Testing W=7: Y = 7+3 (wrap around) = position 3, which is available. So W = 7, Y = 3, leaving D = 2.

 

• Final arrangement (clockwise): B(1), D(2), Y(3), X(4), C(5), A(6), W(7).

 

• Counted from the right (clockwise) of D(2): positions 3, 4 (Y and X) come before reaching C(5) — that is two people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular arrangement puzzles, fix one person's position arbitrarily (e.g., B = 1), convert every 'left/right' clue into a clockwise/anticlockwise position shift, and solve step by step — treating 'right' as clockwise consistently throughout avoids direction confusion.

 

NOTE

 

• 'X people between A and B counted from the right of A' is a directional clue (it matters which of A or B you start counting from) — always count strictly in the specified direction, not the shorter arc.

question:
If 'A' stands for '×', 'B' stands for '÷', 'C' stands for '−' and 'D' stands for '+', what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

14 B 2 D 10 A 5 C 12 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 45.

 

GIVEN

 

• Symbol code: A = ×, B = ÷, C = −, D = +.

 

• Expression: 14 B 2 D 10 A 5 C 12 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the actual symbols: 14 ÷ 2 + 10 × 5 − 12.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 14 ÷ 2 = 7; 10 × 5 = 50.

 

• Now compute: 7 + 50 − 12 = 57 − 12 = 45.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the whole expression with real symbols first (14 ÷ 2 + 10 × 5 − 12), then solve using BODMAS in one pass — never try to substitute and calculate at the same time.

 

NOTE

 

• Division and multiplication are always carried out before addition and subtraction (BODMAS), regardless of the left-to-right order in which the coded letters/symbols originally appeared.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

20 34 21 35 22 36 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 23.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 20, 34, 21, 35, 22, 36, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• The series is made of two interleaved sub-series: odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th...) are 20, 21, 22, ? and even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th...) are 34, 35, 36.

 

• The 1st sub-series increases by 1 each time: 20, 21, 22, so the next term (7th position, the missing term) = 22 + 1 = 23.

 

• (Cross-check: the 2nd sub-series also increases by 1 each time: 34, 35, 36, confirming the overall alternating pattern.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When a series doesn't show an obvious single pattern, check whether it is actually two series interleaved — write alternate terms on two separate lines and look for a pattern in each line independently.

 

NOTE

 

• Here the two interleaved series both increase by +14 alternately from one to the next within the combined series (20→34 is +14, 34→21 is −13... ), but recognising the simpler +1, +1 pattern within each individual sub-series is the fastest route to the answer.

question:
Raghu starts from Point Y and drives 18 km towards west. He then turns right and drives 26 km, takes a left turn, drives 30 km, turns left and drives 68 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 31 km. He takes a right turn, drives 42 km, turns left and drives 16 km to stop at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again?

(All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 95 km towards east.

 

GIVEN

 

• Take east as +x, north as +y. Path from Y: 18 km west; right turn, 26 km; left turn, 30 km; left turn, 68 km; right turn, 31 km; right turn, 42 km; left turn, 16 km, stop at Z.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Y = (0, 0). Drive 18 km west (facing West): (−18, 0).

 

• Right turn from West → facing North. Drive 26 km north: (−18, 26).

 

• Left turn from North → facing West. Drive 30 km west: (−48, 26).

 

• Left turn from West → facing South. Drive 68 km south: (−48, −42).

 

• Right turn from South → facing West. Drive 31 km west: (−79, −42).

 

• Right turn from West → facing North. Drive 42 km north: (−79, 0).

 

• Left turn from North → facing West. Drive 16 km west: (−95, 0). This is Point Z.

 

• Z = (−95, 0), which is 95 km due west of Y = (0, 0). So, to return from Z to Y, Raghu must travel 95 km towards east.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Keep a running total of net east-west (x) and north-south (y) displacement only, updating the facing direction at each turn using the clockwise/anticlockwise rule — here the net y-displacement cancelled to 0, leaving a pure east-west answer.

 

NOTE

 

• The question asks for the direction to return (from Z to Y), which is the exact opposite of the direction Z lies from Y — a frequent trap is to give the direction of Z from Y instead of Y from Z.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). (Counting to be done from left to right only.)

(Left) 1 3 1 8 9 3 1 9 9 3 4 8 6 3 2 4 7 9 5 5 9 7 5 4 1 5 3 (Right)

How many such even numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 1 3 1 8 9 3 1 9 9 3 4 8 6 3 2 4 7 9 5 5 9 7 5 4 1 5 3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan the series for every even number and check whether the number immediately before it is odd AND the number immediately after it is also even.

 

• ...3, 4, 8... → 4 is even, preceded by 3 (odd) ✓, followed by 8 (even) ✓ — this 4 qualifies (1st match).

 

• ...8, 6, 3... → 6 is even, preceded by 8 (even) ✗ — does not qualify.

 

• ...3, 2, 4... → 2 is even, preceded by 3 (odd) ✓, followed by 4 (even) ✓ — this 2 qualifies (2nd match).

 

• ...2, 4, 7... → 4 is even, preceded by 2 (even) ✗ — does not qualify.

 

• ...5, 4, 1... → 4 is even, preceded by 5 (odd) ✓, but followed by 1 (odd) ✗ — does not qualify.

 

• No other even number in the series satisfies both conditions simultaneously, so the total count = 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Go through the series once, underlining every even number; for each underlined number, just glance one step left and one step right to check odd-then-even-then-even — don't re-scan the whole series for each number.

 

NOTE

 

• It's easy to accidentally skip a small single-digit even number like '2' while scanning quickly — read the series slowly, digit by digit, especially around single-digit numbers like 2, 4, 6, 8 that are easy to overlook.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic.

SWAP - WSAP - PAWS

ALSO - LASO - OSLA
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. USER - SUER - RESU.

 

GIVEN

 

• Example 1: SWAP → WSAP → PAWS. Example 2: ALSO → LASO → OSLA.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word 1 → word 2): swap the 1st and 2nd letters. SWAP(S,W,A,P) → WSAP(W,S,A,P) ✓; ALSO(A,L,S,O) → LASO(L,A,S,O) ✓.

 

• Step 2 (word 2 → word 3): reverse the entire word, then swap the last two letters of that reversed word. Reverse(WSAP) = P,A,S,W; swap last two (S,W → W,S) = P,A,W,S = PAWS ✓ matches. Reverse(LASO) = O,S,A,L; swap last two (A,L → L,A) = O,S,L,A = OSLA ✓ matches.

 

• Apply the same two rules to Option D: USER(U,S,E,R) → swap 1st & 2nd → SUER(S,U,E,R) ✓ matches given.

 

• SUER → reverse it: R,E,U,S; swap last two letters (U,S → S,U): R,E,S,U = RESU ✓ matches given third term exactly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Verify the two confirmed rules (swap first two letters; then reverse-and-swap-last-two) directly against each option's given three words — the one option where BOTH transformations check out exactly is the answer; testing this way is faster than re-deriving the rule from scratch each time.

 

NOTE

 

• When a rule is established from two solved examples, always test it fully (both steps) on the given options rather than assuming a partial match (matching only step 1) is sufficient.

question: In a certain code language, 'CORM' is coded as '9518' and 'MORE' is coded as '5831'. What is the code for 'E' in the given code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• CORM → 9518; MORE → 5831.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Compare the two words: CORM has letters {C, O, R, M}; MORE has letters {M, O, R, E}. The letters M, O, R are common to both words, while C is unique to CORM and E is unique to MORE.

 

• Similarly, compare the digit-sets of the codes: CORM's code digits are {9, 5, 1, 8}; MORE's code digits are {5, 8, 3, 1}. The digits 5, 1, 8 are common to both codes, while 9 is unique to CORM's code and 3 is unique to MORE's code.

 

• Since the common letters (M, O, R) must correspond to the common digits (5, 1, 8), the unique letter in each word must correspond to that word's unique digit: C (unique to CORM) ↔ 9, and E (unique to MORE) ↔ 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In 'common letters, common code' puzzles, always identify the letters shared between the two coded words and the digits shared between their codes — whatever digit is 'left over' (not shared) corresponds to whatever letter is 'left over' (not shared).

 

NOTE

 

• This elimination technique works even without knowing the exact letter-to-digit cipher rule, as long as exactly one letter and one digit are uniquely left over after removing the common ones.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some rabbits are fans.

No fan is a car.

Conclusions:

(I): Some rabbits are cars.

(II): Some fans are rabbits.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Only conclusion (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: Some rabbits are fans (particular affirmative, I-type).

 

• Statement 2: No fan is a car (universal negative, E-type).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Conclusion (II), 'Some fans are rabbits', is simply the converse of Statement 1 ('Some rabbits are fans'). Conversion of a particular affirmative (I-type) statement is always logically valid, so Conclusion (II) follows.

 

• Conclusion (I), 'Some rabbits are cars', requires linking 'rabbits' with 'cars' — but combining an I-type premise (Some rabbits are fans) with an E-type premise (No fan is a car) through the common term 'fans' does not yield any valid conclusion connecting rabbits and cars directly (an I + E combination gives, at most, 'Some rabbits are not cars', never 'Some rabbits are cars'). So Conclusion (I) does not follow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw a Venn diagram: a circle for 'fans' with a small overlapping part shared with 'rabbits', and the 'car' circle drawn completely separate from (not touching) the 'fans' circle — this shows 'Some fans are rabbits' is valid, while 'Some rabbits are cars' clearly cannot be read off the diagram.

 

NOTE

 

• A particular affirmative (I-type, 'Some A are B') always converts validly to 'Some B are A' — this is one of the most frequently tested conversion rules in syllogism questions.

question:
Refer to the given number, symbol series and answer the question that follows.

(Left) 7 $ 5 @ 3 ! 3 5 6 7 & % $ 3 # 2 7 + ? > < (Right)

If all the numbers are dropped from the series, which of the following will be seventh from the right?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. %.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 7 $ 5 @ 3 ! 3 5 6 7 & % $ 3 # 2 7 + ? > < .

 

SOLUTION

 

• Remove all the numbers (7, 5, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 3, 2, 7) from the series, keeping only the symbols in their original left-to-right order.

 

• Remaining symbols, in order: $, @, !, &, %, $, #, +, ?, >, < (11 symbols in total).

 

• Counting from the right: 1st = <, 2nd = >, 3rd = ?, 4th = +, 5th = #, 6th = $, 7th = %.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• After removing the specified elements (here, numbers), rewrite only the remaining elements as a fresh, compact list — then simply count from the required end (left or right) on this shorter list, rather than trying to count within the original, longer series.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check whether the question asks to count 'from the left' or 'from the right' of the reduced series — this is the most common source of an off-by-position error in such questions.

question: Srinivas ranked 2nd from the top and 19th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in the class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 20.

 

GIVEN

 

• Srinivas's rank = 2nd from the top; also 19th from the bottom.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total number of students = (Rank from top) + (Rank from bottom) − 1.

 

• Total students = 2 + 19 − 1 = 20.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always subtract 1 (since Srinivas himself is counted once in both the 'from top' and 'from bottom' ranks) — the formula Total = Top rank + Bottom rank − 1 applies to any such ranking question.

 

NOTE

 

• A very common mistake is to simply add the two ranks (2 + 19 = 21) and forget to subtract 1 for the person being double-counted.

question: In a certain code language, 'LOVE' is coded as '4958' and 'VALE' is coded as '3589'. What is the code for 'A' in the given code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• LOVE → 4958; VALE → 3589.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Compare the letters: LOVE has {L, O, V, E}; VALE has {V, A, L, E}. The letters L, V, E are common to both words; O is unique to LOVE and A is unique to VALE.

 

• Compare the digit-sets: LOVE's code digits are {4, 9, 5, 8}; VALE's code digits are {3, 5, 8, 9}. The digits 9, 5, 8 are common to both codes; 4 is unique to LOVE's code and 3 is unique to VALE's code.

 

• Matching unique-to-unique: O (unique to LOVE) ↔ 4, and A (unique to VALE) ↔ 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Exactly as with any 'two coded words sharing some letters' question: strip out the letters (and digits) common to both words/codes first — whatever single letter and single digit remain unmatched on each side must correspond to each other.

 

NOTE

 

• This method only requires that exactly one letter differs between the two given words (or is uniquely left over after removing common letters) — always verify this condition holds before applying the shortcut.

question: TQKG is related to XUOK in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, SPJF is related to WTNJ. To which of the given options is ROIE related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. VSMI.

 

GIVEN

 

• TQKG is related to XUOK; SPJF is related to WTNJ (both following the same alphabetical-position logic).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the rule using alphabet positions: T(20)→X(24): +4; Q(17)→U(21): +4; K(11)→O(15): +4; G(7)→K(11): +4. So each letter of TQKG is shifted forward by 4 places to get XUOK.

 

• Verify with the second pair: S(19)→W(23): +4; P(16)→T(20): +4; J(10)→N(14): +4; F(6)→J(10): +4 — confirms the same +4 shift rule.

 

• Apply the same +4 shift to ROIE: R(18)→V(22); O(15)→S(19); I(9)→M(13); E(5)→I(9). This gives V, S, M, I = VSMI.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With two worked examples given, verify the exact numeric shift (here, always +4) using just the first letters of each pair, then apply that same shift to all four letters of the new word directly using alphabet positions (A=1...Z=26).

 

NOTE

 

• If a shifted letter's position exceeds 26, wrap around by subtracting 26 (e.g., position 27 becomes A); this wasn't needed here since all shifted positions stayed within 1-26.

question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

(Left) 316 562 149 379 433 (Right)

(Example: 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

(NOTE: All operations to be done from left to right.)

What will be the resultant if the second digit of the highest number is added to the third digit of the lowest number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 15.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers: 316, 562, 149, 379, 433.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The highest number among these is 562; its second digit is 6.

 

• The lowest number among these is 149; its third digit is 9.

 

• Required resultant = second digit of highest number + third digit of lowest number = 6 + 9 = 15.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First identify only the highest and lowest numbers from the given list by simple comparison, then pick out just the specific digit asked for from each — no need to analyse the digits of the other three numbers at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Digit positions are always counted from the left (1st digit = hundreds place, 2nd = tens place, 3rd = units place) as clarified by the example given in the question — always check such example notes carefully before answering.

question: If 1 is added to each odd digit and 2 is subtracted from each even digit in the number 4651783. What will be the sum of the highest digit and the second from the left and first from the right in the new number thus formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 16.

 

GIVEN

 

• Original number: 4 6 5 1 7 8 3. Rule: add 1 to each odd digit; subtract 2 from each even digit.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Apply the rule digit by digit: 4(even)→4−2=2; 6(even)→6−2=4; 5(odd)→5+1=6; 1(odd)→1+1=2; 7(odd)→7+1=8; 8(even)→8−2=6; 3(odd)→3+1=4.

 

• New number formed: 2 4 6 2 8 6 4.

 

• Highest digit in the new number = 8.

 

• Second digit from the left = 4; first digit from the right (i.e., the last digit) = 4.

 

• Required sum = 8 + 4 + 4 = 16.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Apply the odd/even rule to each digit in one careful left-to-right pass and write out the complete new number first — then answer the position-based questions (highest digit, Nth from left/right) by simply reading off this new number, rather than trying to track positions and value-changes simultaneously.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember that 0 counts as an even digit (subtract 2, which could make it negative in other questions) — always re-check each digit's parity (odd/even) carefully before applying the rule.

question:
Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

(Left) ? * + ? \ & 3 # 9 % 4 1 6 * @ 5 4 8 8 $ \ (Right)

How many such numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by another number and also immediately followed by a symbol?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: ? * + ? \ & 3 # 9 % 4 1 6 * @ 5 4 8 8 $ \ (with '?' and '\' used here simply as two of the symbol characters in the series).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Identify the numbers in the series with their neighbours: ...**% 4 1 6 * ... and ...@ 5 4 8 8 $...**.

 

• Check '4' (before '1'): preceded by % (symbol) — does not qualify (needs to be preceded by a number).

 

• Check '1' (between 4 and 6): preceded by 4 (number) ✓, followed by 6 (number) ✗ — does not qualify (needs to be followed by a symbol).

 

• Check '6' (before '*'): preceded by 1 (number) ✓, followed by * (symbol) ✓ — qualifies (1st match).

 

• Check '5' (after @): preceded by @ (symbol) — does not qualify.

 

• Check '4' (after 5): preceded by 5 (number) ✓, followed by 8 (number) ✗ — does not qualify.

question:
Which of the given letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the following series to make it logically complete?

ECP 1 GEM −2 IGJ 4 KIG −8 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. MKD 16.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: ECP, 1, GEM, −2, IGJ, 4, KIG, −8, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• The numbers between clusters follow the pattern: 1, −2, 4, −8 — each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by −2: 1×(−2)=−2; −2×(−2)=4; 4×(−2)=−8; so the next number = −8×(−2) = 16.

 

• For the letter clusters, split into 1st, 2nd and 3rd letters (using A=1...Z=26): 1st letters: E(5), G(7), I(9), K(11) → +2 each → next = 13 = M.

 

• 2nd letters: C(3), E(5), G(7), I(9) → +2 each → next = 11 = K.

 

• 3rd letters: P(16), M(13), J(10), G(7) → −3 each → next = 4 = D.

 

• Missing cluster = MKD, missing number = 16, giving MKD 16.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Separate the alternating letter-clusters and numbers into two independent series first — solve the simple geometric-progression number pattern (×(−2) each time) separately from the column-wise letter pattern, then combine the two answers at the end.

 

NOTE

 

• A repeating ×(−2) pattern in numbers causes the sign to flip every term (positive, negative, positive, negative...) — always double check the sign of the next term, not just its magnitude.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

10, 23, 49, 88, 140, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 205.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 10, 23, 49, 88, 140, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the first differences: 23−10=13; 49−23=26; 88−49=39; 140−88=52.

 

• These differences (13, 26, 39, 52) increase by a constant 13 each time, so the next difference = 52 + 13 = 65.

 

• Next term = 140 + 65 = 205.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Notice the differences themselves are multiples of 13 (13, 26=13×2, 39=13×3, 52=13×4), so the next difference is simply 13×5 = 65 — recognising this pattern lets you skip writing out the subtraction each time.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever a series' differences form their own simple arithmetic (or multiple-based) pattern, always extend that inner pattern one more step before adding it to the last term of the original series.

question: Seven boxes A, B, C, D, I, J and K are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. K is kept second from the bottom. Only three boxes are kept between K and I. D is kept at one of the positions below K. Only B is kept between I and J. A is kept at one of the positions above I. How many boxes are kept between C and D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes stacked in positions 1 (bottom) to 7 (top). K is 2nd from the bottom; 3 boxes between K and I; D is below K; only B between I and J; A is above I.

 

SOLUTION

 

• K is 2nd from bottom ⇒ K = position 2.

 

• Only 3 boxes between K(2) and I ⇒ |position(I) − 2| − 1 = 3 ⇒ position(I) = 6 (since −2 is invalid) ⇒ I = position 6.

 

• D is below K(2) ⇒ the only position below 2 is 1 ⇒ D = position 1.

 

• Only B between I(6) and J ⇒ |position(J) − 6| − 1 = 1 ⇒ position(J) = 4 (since 8 is invalid) ⇒ J = position 4; the single box between I(6) and J(4) is position 5, so B = position 5.

 

• A is above I(6) ⇒ the only position above 6 (excluding 6 itself and already-used 7... actually 7 is the only slot above 6) ⇒ A = position 7.

 

• Remaining position 3 goes to C.

 

• Final arrangement (bottom to top): D(1), K(2), C(3), J(4), B(5), I(6), A(7).

 

• Number of boxes between C(3) and D(1) = the box at position 2 (K) only = one box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the absolute positions from the most specific clues first (K = 2nd from bottom, D below K), then use the 'N boxes between' clues to pin down further positions one at a time — leaving only one box (C) to be found by elimination at the very end.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Kept at one of the positions below/above X' with only one remaining valid slot effectively fixes that box's position exactly — treat such clues as precise once other positions are known, not just as a loose direction.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: the odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. BF-IE.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pairs: DH-KF, FJ-MH, HL-OJ, BF-IE (using A=1...Z=26).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the shift pattern for each pair (1st letter → 1st letter, and 2nd letter → 2nd letter):

 

• DH-KF: D(4)→K(11): +7; H(8)→F(6): −2.

 

• FJ-MH: F(6)→M(13): +7; J(10)→H(8): −2.

 

• HL-OJ: H(8)→O(15): +7; L(12)→J(10): −2.

 

• BF-IE: B(2)→I(9): +7 (consistent), but F(6)→E(5): only −1, not −2 as in the other three pairs.

 

• Since DH-KF, FJ-MH and HL-OJ all follow the same '+7, −2' rule while BF-IE follows '+7, −1', BF-IE is the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Compute the alphabet-position shift for both letters in each pair quickly, and look for the pair whose second-letter shift breaks the otherwise consistent pattern shown by the other three — a difference of just 1 in a single shift value is enough to expose the odd one out.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the pattern using all four pairs before concluding — a rule that looks consistent for the first two or three pairs can still break down in the fourth, as seen here.

solution_text:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once you find a consistent '+7 on the first letter, +3 on the second letter' rule from three pairs, apply it to the fourth and watch carefully for wrap-around (mod 26) cases — a wrap-around mismatch of even a single letter (C vs D here) is often exactly how the odd one out is disguised.

 

NOTE

 

• When a shifted alphabet position exceeds 26, subtract 26 to wrap back to the start (A=1); a common trap in these questions is when the 'expected' wrapped letter is off by one or two from the option actually given.

• I. M. Vijayan, the legendary former Indian football striker often called the 'Kerala Express' or 'Black Pearl', was conferred the Padma Shri in 2025 in recognition of his outstanding contribution to Indian football. (आई.एम. विजयन — पद्म श्री 2025)

 

• Vijayan was one of India's most prolific strikers in the 1990s and early 2000s, representing the Indian national team and playing a key role in India's football successes during that era, including SAFF Championship triumphs.

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, conferred by the President of India for distinguished contributions in various fields, including sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are given in three categories in descending order of importance: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri, announced every year on the eve of Republic Day (26 January).

 

• Other legendary Indian footballers honoured in the past with Padma awards include Bhaichung Bhutia (Padma Shri) and P.K. Banerjee.

 

• I.M. Vijayan was also honoured earlier with the Arjuna Award for his footballing achievements.

 

NOTE

 

• Sandesh Jhingan (Option B): A current Indian international defender, an important modern-day player, but not the 2025 Padma Shri recipient referred to here.

 

• Sunil Chhetri (Option C): India's iconic captain and record goal-scorer, already honoured with the Padma Shri (2019) and Padma Bhushan (2021) in earlier years, but not the specific 2025 recipient in this question.

 

• Bhaichung Bhutia (Option D): A football legend and earlier Padma Shri (2008) recipient, but not the player awarded in 2025 as referenced here.

question: India joined which European drone programme as an observer in January 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eurodrone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India joined the Eurodrone programme as an observer in January 2025, marking a step towards greater defence-technology cooperation with European partners. (यूरोड्रोन कार्यक्रम — भारत पर्यवेक्षक के रूप में शामिल)

 

• The Eurodrone (European MALE RPAS) programme is a joint European initiative to develop a Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) Remotely Piloted Aircraft System, involving countries such as Germany, France, Italy and Spain.

 

• India's observer status allows it to engage with and learn from the European consortium's drone development efforts, complementing India's own indigenous drone and UAV development programmes under initiatives like Atmanirbhar Bharat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has been steadily building its own drone ecosystem, supporting indigenous manufacturers under schemes like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for drones, alongside procurement of platforms like the American MQ-9B Predator drones.

 

• Defence cooperation between India and European nations has been expanding in recent years, covering areas such as fighter aircraft engines, submarines and now unmanned systems.

 

• DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation) leads India's indigenous UAV development, including platforms like the Rustom series and the Tapas drone.

 

NOTE

 

• Global Hawk (Option A): A long-endurance American surveillance drone (Northrop Grumman), not a European programme.

 

• Predator XP (Option B): A variant of the American General Atomics Predator drone family, not a European programme.

 

• nEUROn (Option C): A European unmanned combat air vehicle (UCAV) demonstrator project led by France (Dassault Aviation) with other European partners, distinct from the Eurodrone MALE programme that India joined as an observer.

question: In August 2025, Union Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava, virtually inaugurated an innovative national mechanism aimed at evaluating and improving state drug regulatory frameworks through an open and evidence-based approach named ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is State Health Regulatory Excellence Index.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In August 2025, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava virtually inaugurated the State Health Regulatory Excellence Index, a national mechanism designed to evaluate and improve state drug regulatory frameworks through an open, transparent and evidence-based ranking approach. (राज्य स्वास्थ्य नियामक उत्कृष्टता सूचकांक)

 

• The index is intended to benchmark and compare the performance of different states' drug regulatory systems, encouraging states to strengthen their regulatory processes, drug quality control, and enforcement mechanisms.

 

• Such indices are part of India's broader cooperative and competitive federalism approach, where ranking states on governance parameters (similar to indices for health, education, or ease of doing business) is used to drive reforms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Drug regulation in India operates at both the central level (Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, CDSCO) and the state level (State Drug Control Departments), making coordination and benchmarking between states important for consistent drug quality and safety standards nationwide.

 

• The Union Health Ministry has periodically launched similar ranking or index-based initiatives in the health sector to encourage evidence-based policymaking, such as the NITI Aayog Health Index for overall state health system performance.

 

• Strengthening drug regulatory frameworks is critical for ensuring the safety, efficacy and quality of medicines manufactured and sold across India, given India's status as a major global pharmaceutical manufacturing hub.

 

NOTE

 

• National Drug Regulatory Reform Index, Health Infrastructure Performance Index and Pharmaceutical Compliance Monitoring Index (Options A, B and D): These are plausible-sounding names, but the actual mechanism inaugurated in August 2025 for evaluating state drug regulatory frameworks was named the State Health Regulatory Excellence Index.

question: Who took office as the Deputy Governor of the RBI on 2 April 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poonam Gupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Poonam Gupta, an economist, took office as a Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on 2 April 2025, joining the RBI's top leadership team. (पूनम गुप्ता — RBI डिप्टी गवर्नर)

 

• Prior to this appointment, Poonam Gupta had a distinguished background in economic research and policy, having been associated with institutions such as the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) and international bodies like the World Bank.

 

• The RBI Deputy Governors oversee key policy areas such as monetary policy, banking regulation, currency management and financial stability, working under the overall leadership of the RBI Governor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• As of 2025, the RBI Governor was Sanjay Malhotra, who succeeded Shaktikanta Das.

 

• The RBI typically has four Deputy Governors at a time — usually including one from the RBI's own cadre, one from commercial banking, and others from fields like economics and regulation.

 

• The RBI plays a central role in India's economy through functions such as setting the repo rate via the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), regulating banks and NBFCs, and managing foreign exchange reserves.

 

NOTE

 

• Michael Debroy (Option A): Not a recognised RBI official; this appears to be a distractor name.

 

• Michael Patra (Option B): A former RBI Deputy Governor known for his role in monetary policy, but his term as Deputy Governor concluded before this April 2025 appointment.

 

• Ashwani Bhatia (Option D): A SEBI Whole-Time Member around this period, not the RBI Deputy Governor appointed on 2 April 2025.

question: What are the revised investment caps for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) in corporate bonds for FY 2025-26, as announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in April 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in April 2025, announced the revised investment limit for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) in corporate bonds for FY 2025-26 at 15% of outstanding stock, as part of its regular annual review of FPI investment limits. (FPI निवेश सीमा — कॉर्पोरेट बॉन्ड में 15%)

 

• FPI investment limits in Indian debt markets (both government securities and corporate bonds) are reviewed and set annually by the RBI in consultation with the government, expressed as a percentage of the outstanding stock of the relevant securities.

 

• These limits are intended to manage the pace and scale of foreign capital flows into India's debt markets, balancing the benefits of foreign investment with financial stability considerations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• FPI limits are typically set separately for different categories, such as government securities (G-Secs), state development loans (SDLs), and corporate bonds, and are reviewed at the start of each financial year (April).

 

• India's debt markets have also seen growing global interest following India's inclusion in major global bond indices, such as the JPMorgan Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets (GBI-EM), which has boosted foreign inflows into Indian government securities.

 

• The RBI regulates FPI investments under the framework set out in consultation with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and the government.

 

NOTE

 

• 12%, 18% and 10% (Options A, C and D): These do not match the revised FPI investment cap of 15% in corporate bonds announced by the RBI for FY 2025-26.

question: Which country's authorities were flagged by India in 2025 for hybrid cannabis smuggling via couriers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thailand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India flagged concerns to Thailand's authorities in 2025 regarding the smuggling of hybrid cannabis into India via couriers/postal and parcel channels, highlighting a growing trend of narcotics trafficking exploiting international courier networks. (हाइब्रिड गांजा तस्करी — थाईलैंड)

 

• Hybrid cannabis refers to genetically bred/cross-strain cannabis varieties with higher potency, which have become an increasing concern for drug-enforcement agencies globally due to their higher THC content and market demand.

 

• India's law enforcement and customs agencies, such as the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), have been working to intercept such smuggling attempts and have engaged in diplomatic/enforcement coordination with source countries to curb the trend.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Thailand decriminalised cannabis for medical and personal use in 2022, which has led to a boom in its domestic cannabis industry — but this has also been linked to concerns about cannabis being illegally exported/smuggled to countries like India where it remains a banned narcotic substance.

 

• India's Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985 governs the control and regulation of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in the country.

 

• International cooperation on narcotics control is coordinated through bodies such as INTERPOL and bilateral agreements between drug-enforcement agencies of different countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Nigeria, Myanmar and Afghanistan (Options B, C and D): All are countries associated with other forms of narcotics trafficking concerns (e.g., Myanmar's Golden Triangle heroin/methamphetamine trade, Afghanistan's opium production), but the specific hybrid-cannabis-via-courier smuggling concern flagged by India in 2025 was linked to Thailand.

question: What was India's rank in the Global Innovation Index (GII), 2025, released by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 38th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India ranked 38th in the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025, released by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), continuing its steady improvement in global innovation rankings over the past several years. (वैश्विक नवाचार सूचकांक 2025 — भारत 38वें स्थान पर)

 

• The GII ranks countries based on around 80 indicators covering areas such as institutions, human capital and research, infrastructure, market sophistication, business sophistication, and knowledge & technology outputs.

 

• India's rise up the GII rankings over the past decade (from around 81st in 2015 to 38th in 2025) reflects growing investment in research, start-ups, digital infrastructure and innovation-driven policy under initiatives like Startup India and Atal Innovation Mission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The GII is published annually by WIPO, a specialised agency of the United Nations responsible for promoting intellectual property protection worldwide, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

 

• India has consistently been recognised in GII reports as a top innovation performer relative to its income group (lower-middle-income economies), and for strengths in areas like ICT services exports and the quality of its scientific publications.

 

• Switzerland, Sweden, the United States and other developed economies typically occupy the top ranks of the GII, reflecting their strong innovation ecosystems.

 

NOTE

 

• 43rd, 33rd and 28th (Options A, B and C): These are close but incorrect figures; India's actual rank in the GII 2025 was 38th.

question: Which Indian javelin thrower won the Ostrava Golden Spike event in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neeraj Chopra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neeraj Chopra, India's Olympic and World Champion javelin thrower, won the Ostrava Golden Spike athletics event in 2025, adding another prestigious international title to his career. (नीरज चोपड़ा — ओस्ट्रावा गोल्डन स्पाइक)

 

• The Golden Spike (Zlatá tretra) is a well-known annual athletics meeting held in Ostrava, Czech Republic, and forms part of the global World Athletics Continental Tour, attracting elite athletes from around the world.

 

• Neeraj Chopra remains India's most decorated track-and-field athlete, having won the gold medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, silver at the Paris 2024 Olympics, and the World Athletics Championship gold in 2023, alongside numerous Diamond League and other international meet victories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Neeraj Chopra hails from Panipat, Haryana, and became the first Indian track-and-field athlete to win an Olympic gold medal at Tokyo 2020.

 

• He has also launched the Neeraj Chopra Classic, a javelin-focused international athletics event held in India, aimed at promoting the sport domestically.

 

• Other prominent Indian javelin throwers on the international circuit include Kishore Jena and Annu Rani (India's leading woman javelin thrower).

 

NOTE

 

• Kishore Kumar (Option A): Not a recognised Indian javelin thrower; likely a distractor name (possibly confused with athlete Kishore Jena).

 

• Rohit Yadav (Option B): An emerging Indian javelin thrower who has competed at national and international levels, but not the winner of the Ostrava Golden Spike 2025 referenced here.

 

• Annu Rani (Option C): India's top woman javelin thrower and Asian Games medallist, but the men's event winner referred to in this question is Neeraj Chopra.

question: Which of the following schemes announced a financial outlay of ₹5,000 crore to promote research & innovation in the pharmaceutical and med-tech sectors in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PRIP scheme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The PRIP scheme (Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma-MedTech Sector) announced a financial outlay of ₹5,000 crore to boost research and innovation in India's pharmaceutical and medical technology (med-tech) sectors. (PRIP योजना — फार्मा-मेडटेक अनुसंधान हेतु ₹5,000 करोड़)

 

• The scheme, run under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, aims to support research infrastructure, innovation centres, and collaborative research in critical areas like complex generics, biosimilars, novel drug delivery systems, orphan drugs and medical devices.

 

• The PRIP scheme is part of India's broader strategy to reduce dependence on imports for high-value pharmaceutical research and to strengthen India's position as a global hub not just for drug manufacturing, but also for pharmaceutical innovation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is often called the 'pharmacy of the world' due to its position as a leading global supplier of generic medicines and vaccines, and the PRIP scheme aims to extend this leadership into innovation-led, high-value research.

 

• Other government schemes supporting the pharma sector include the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for pharmaceuticals and schemes to promote bulk drug parks and medical device parks.

 

• The National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER) network plays a key role in supporting pharmaceutical research and skill development in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Smart Cities Mission (Option A): A government initiative focused on urban infrastructure and technology-driven city development, unrelated to pharma/med-tech research.

 

• Startup India (Option B): A broader initiative to promote entrepreneurship and start-ups across sectors, not specifically the ₹5,000 crore pharma-med-tech research scheme referenced here.

 

• Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (Option C): India's broad self-reliance economic initiative covering many sectors, under which schemes like PRIP may fall conceptually, but the specific ₹5,000 crore pharma-med-tech research scheme itself is named the PRIP scheme.
